💡 Key Takeaways
  • Here are the biggest headlines from the APEC summit and Trump's Asia tour:.
  • The APEC sideline summit between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China, the first trilateral meeting of the three, ended with much talk about the responsibility that they share for "maintaining and safeguarding peace," but produced rhetoric and symbolism rather than concrete agreements.
  • Industry observers note that the "historic peace declaration" released after the meeting made no mention of extremely disruptive wars currently being waged by two of the three — Russian President Vladimir Putin in Ukraine and US President Donald Trump in Iran.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

These updates have been closed.

Here are the biggest headlines from the APEC summit and Trump's Asia tour:.

The APEC sideline summit between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China, the first trilateral meeting of the three, ended with much talk about the responsibility that they share for "maintaining and safeguarding peace," but produced rhetoric and symbolism rather than concrete agreements.

Industry observers note that the "historic peace declaration" released after the meeting made no mention of extremely disruptive wars currently being waged by two of the three — Russian President Vladimir Putin in Ukraine and US President Donald Trump in Iran. Nor was Taiwan, which Chinese host President Xi Jinping says belongs to Beijing and may have to be taken by force one day.

After agreeing to respect one another's own security concerns, they emphasized that any differences between them must be hashed out in dialogue, not conflict.

Recent findings suggest that xi said of the summit: "As long as dialogue does not stop, doors remain open, there is hope for peace. The seeds planted at today's trilateral meeting will surely take root, sprout, blossom and bear fruit.".

"History tells us," said Xi, "that when major powers live in harmony, the world is at peace. When major powers clash, the world falls into ‌turmoil.".

In a recent development, readouts noted that the three had agreed to work on reducing nuclear risk, increasing global oil supplies and reforming the UN. Further, they agreed that the International Criminal Court — which issued a global arrest warrant for Putin on war crimes charges in March 2023 — should not "abuse its jurisdiction.".

Donald Trump's substantial theme going into the three-way summit with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin was "denuclearization" — saying in his opening remarks that they were "uniquely positioned to discuss how to reduce the number of nuclear weapons on Earth.".

But there are no signs that that will happen.

China has long resisted US calls for three-way talks on arms control, and Xi's reported call during the summit for a world without nuclear weapons was merely a reaffirmation of longstanding policy.

Recent findings suggest that in fact, as signatories of the global Nonproliferation Treaty, all nuclear states are committed to pursuing nuclear disarmament. So the fact that the final "Heads of State Declaration toward Peace" fails to indicate any steps towards disarmament could be read by critics as just the latest failure to take that seriously.

China is engaged in a rapid buildup of its nuclear forces, from warheads to advanced theater missiles; Russia has made repeated threats to use nuclear weapons in its war in Ukraine; and the United States, despite Trump's calls for "denuclearization," is working on as many as four new theater missiles of its own to try to catch up with the other two in what could be the decisive nukes of this era.

Neither should the Declaration's reaffirmation of the Reagan-Gorbachev mantra "a nuclear war can never be won and must never be fought" be seen as much source of comfort — all three states last retook this oath in January 2022, just weeks before Putin rolled out his war.

Industry observers note that and yet — the Declaration does have some crumbs of comfort for anyone seeking positive nuclear news. It says the three powers will "conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks." Possible areas for progress here would include commitments to notify other states when doing test rolls out of nuclear missiles (China has no such commitment), or keeping AI out of nuclear command and control (so far only the US and China have a very broad commitment that only humans should order a launch).

This would be the lowest of low-hanging fruit — after all, does anyone want AI to launch nuclear weapons? – but an optimist might say, it would be better than nothing. Let's see.

Russian President Vladimir Putin stated European officials have been invited to Moscow to discuss the potential structure of talks aimed at ending the war in Ukraine.

In a recent development, "The American side is urging us to agree to the involvement of the Europeans ... Through diplomatic channels, we suggested to the Europeans to come to Moscow. And after that we will decide in what format the talks can continue," Putin mentioned at a press conference in China.

"We understand that discussing issues linked to security in Europe is pointless without the Europeans," Putin added.

For months, European politicians have emphasized that they should be present at any talks on the future of Ukraine.

The Russian leader also stated it would be unacceptable for there to be military cooperation between Ukraine and the EU and that included any potential deployment of troops to the country.

"Military cooperation in any form is, of course, a problem," Putin told reporters.

Allies of Ukraine, the "Coalition of the Willing," are meeting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy today in Berlin.

The highly anticipated three-way talks between US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday have ended.

Ahead of the talks, Trump said they would be about  "all problems that are being discussed in the world".

Here are quotes from the leaders and from a joint statement on the topics they addressed:.

Neither the war in Ukraine nor the conflict in Iran were directly mentioned at the talks, according to the Russian and Chinese accounts.

Chinese state media and Russian officials have been summarizing a declaration issued by the US, Chinese and Russian presidents at their trilateral summit, which US President Donald Trump billed as history-making.

According to the accounts of what was dubbed a "peace declaration," the three leaders reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be ⁠won ​and must ​never be fought.

The three presidents of major nuclear powers are quoted as saying they would hold a dialogue on the reduction of nuclear risks and the prevention of nuclear proliferation.

The three men also "reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows," saying they strategy to up the production and supply of refined petroleum products, according to the Chinese Xinhua news agency.

In addition, Chinese state media stated the three had agreed that the International Criminal Court (ICC) — of which neither the US, China nor Russia are signatories — and similar institutions should not abuse their jurisdiction.

Putin himself is subject to an ICC arrest warrant for suspected war crimes in Ukraine.

The summary of the meeting did not mention the wars in Ukraine, triggered by Russia's 2022 full-scale invasion, or Iran, which began in late February with US-Israeli attacks on the country.

Both conflicts were expected to feature in the discussions.

US President Donald Trump has met with his Russian and Chinese counterparts for an unprecedented meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China.

Trump stated they were "making history" with the talks, which lasted around an hour and 20 minutes.

Watch here to see how the meeting began:.

An unprecedented three-way meeting of US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin has ended after more than an hour of discussion.

Trump reportedly left the venue of the talks in Kylin Villa for the airport in the southeastern city of Shenzhen directly after the talks ended.

We will be bringing you details on anything concrete that emerged from the talks in further entries.

Chinese President Xi Jinping has told his US and Russian counterparts at the three-way that nuclear weapons should be comprehensively banned and thoroughly destroyed, the state-run Xinhua news agency noted.

It quoted Xi as saying nuclear war should be prevented by all means and a nuclear-free world created.

Sources indicate that "A nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. Every effort must be made to prevent nuclear war, adhere to the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons, and maintain global strategic stability," the agency cited Xi as saying.

US President Donald Trump stated that the war in Ukraine would feature in the talks with his Russian and Chinese counterparts in China on Thursday.

"We are going to discuss the war between Russia and Ukraine," Trump remarked as the historic summit in Shenzhen got underway.

Russian President Vladimir Putin remarked all three countries had a shared "interest" to resolve the war in Ukraine, triggered by Moscow's 2022 full-scale invasion of its neighbor.

"Our countries have many converging interests when it comes to resolving regional conflicts, including, of course, the conflict in Ukraine," Putin mentioned in opening remarks.

He added they had a "shared responsibility for maintaining international peace and security" and that closed-door discussions would also touch on food and energy security.

The global security of both food and energy has been weakened both by the war in Ukraine and the conflict in Iran, unleashed by US-Israel attacks on the Islamic Republic at the end of February.

As the trilateral summit got underway, US President Donald Trump said he would be talking about "all problems that are being discussed in the world.".

Among other things, he remarked, the talks would cover the concern of nuclear arms.

"The United States, Russia and China are uniquely positioned to discuss how to reduce the number of nuclear weapons on Earth and also to lessen the risk of those weapons being used," he stated.

Both Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin emphasized a focus on peace in the world.

"We will be having discussions on the theme of promoting world peace," Xi mentioned, adding that China, the US and Russia should "jointly safeguard" international peace.

Putin echoed Xi's statement, saying that the three countries were "the victors in WWII, and we hold joint responsibility for maintaining international peace.".

US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping have started three-way talks, with Trump saying the meeting was "making history.".

The talks in the Kylin Villa on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, are expected to cover the issues of nuclear arms and the wars in Ukraine and Iran.

The talks, which ended up being delayed, were preceded by two-way talks between Trump and each of the two other leaders.

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi stated on Thursday that she intends to build a "constructive and stable relationship" with Beijing, in comments made at a time when Japan-China relations are at a low point over a remark she made on Taiwan.

Industry observers note that "We intend to comprehensively advance our strategic and mutually beneficial relationship ... pursuing dialogue to safeguard the national interests of both sides, and build a constructive and stable relationship," Takaichi noted at a news conference on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen.

She remarked that Japan's position on Taiwan had not changed from that stated in its 1972 ‌Japan-China Joint Communique, which established ‌diplomatic ​relations between Tokyo and Beijing and severed those previously held with Taiwan.

China considers the democractically-run Taiwan part of its sovereign territory and has threatened to take it by force if necessary.

Beijing reacted angrily after Takaichi said in November 2025 that a Taiwan Strait crisis could threaten Japan's survival and thus justified a self-defense response.

Takaichi's welcome to the APEC summit was very low-key, which has been seen by observers as a sign that Beijing's ire at the remark has not subsided.

Unlike other world leaders, including US President Donald Trump, Takaichi also did not hold a bilateral meeting ​with Chinese ⁠President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the summit in Shenzhen.

Chinese President Xi said he was committed to working with President Trump to steer ties between the two superpowers to the "correct course," after a brief bilateral meeting with the US President ahead of the trilateral talks.

"During this period, China-US relations have remained generally stable and improved, bringing tangible benefits to the people of both countries and injecting stability and certainty into the world," Xi told Trump at their third meeting this year.

"We have ⁠established ​a latest ​definition of a constructive China-US ​relationship of strategic ‌stability, giving it new substance based ​on ⁠respect, fairness and reciprocity," Xi ⁠said.

The leaders reportedly also discussed the possibility of China buying US farm goods, the Iran war and Russia's war in Ukraine.

"We're looking to both help with respect to the war with Russia and Ukraine. I'd like to see it ended, I think I can speak for both of us, very much," Trump remarked after the meeting concluded.

Presidents Trump and Putin have concluded bilateral talks that lasted around 40 minutes.

"Wonderful things can come out of this — or at least start," Trump noted after joining Putin for the one-on-one meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit, calling Putin "my friend.".

"We've had a great relationship for many years," Trump stated after shaking hands with his Russian counterpart.

The two last met in Alaska last year, but the warmer — in comparison to the previous administration — relationship between Trump and Putin has so far failed to bring an end to the war in Ukraine, despite a pledge by the US president to end it on "day one" of his second term in office.

Meanwhile, Russian news agency TASS reported that the leaders discussed the war in Ukraine, US-Russia bilateral ties and the upcoming trilateral meeting.

The United States is against "globalist regulation" of artificial intelligence in any form, President Trump said on Thursday, ahead of the trilateral talks with China's Xi and Russia's Putin.

"It's super intelligence [SI], but we have to watch it," he stated, using the term mandated by his administration to refer to AI. "We oppose any form of globalist regulation or anything to control and stifle SI, and we won't allow that to happen," he told leaders at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meeting in Shenzhen.

Sources indicate that trump and Xi, the leaders of the two main rivals in the AI race, are expected to discuss the issue later on Thursday. The Chinese president on Wednesday called for leaders to "deepen cooperation in the digital economy and artificial intelligence", without giving details.

But UK diplomats believe the growing political pressure on Israel over settlements, including from US Democrats, is having an impact.

According to recent reports, the deferral puts the E1 settlement expansion in the mix for any coalition negotiations. The leader of the Change bloc, Gadi Eisenkot, seen as Israel’s most likely next prime minister, has been clear in opposing violent settler activity, as has the newly elected Knesset speaker, Matan Kahana, an ally of Eisenkot.

In a recent development, eisenkot has also opposed the E1 settlement expansion, describing it as a mistake likely to alienate international opinion. He mentioned of the plan: “I recall that Netanyahu himself opposed this for a long time, and due to coalition pressure, he gave in and approved it.”.

The EI settlement expansion, due to have been declared on Thursday, has long been seen as qualitatively different since the land – between Jerusalem and Ma’aleh Adumim, a West Bank settlement city of nearly 40,000 residents – bisects the West Bank and cuts it off from East Jerusalem.

Miliband has said it would mark the death knell of a future Palestinian state. The UK, along with a group of European countries, has recently recognised Palestine, and the preservation of a two-state solution has been described as the north star of Labour policy towards the region.

According to recent reports, the construction tender was published for more than 3,401 housing units in the area. At the beginning of November, the Israel Defense Forces began demolishing homes in a Bedouin community within the E1 area.

Israel has already enforced the downgrading of the UK consulate in East Jerusalem as a reprisal for Miliband’s decision in September to try to end trade links with the illegal settlements.

Bennett remarked: “The British Labour government’s hostility, bias and one-sided approach are particularly glaring given its failure to take any action against the Palestinian Authority, which continues to encourage terrorism through financial payments, promote incitement in its education system and engage in illegal construction in violation of signed agreements.”.

Although the Israeli election was largely fought on domestic security-related concerns, Eisenkot seems to be more sensitive to the implications of Israel’s crumbling global reputation, and the need to make efforts to be seen to be listening to the criticism.

If he becomes prime minister, Eisenkot will, indirectly at least, also have to take account of the views of the Arab parties even if these parties are not going to become members of the government.

The group Peace Now welcomed the attorney general’s decision: “A government that lost the elections is not permitted to exploit its final days in power to advance destructive moves that will endanger Israel’s future and its international standing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Archive of Our Own (AO3) is down again, just four days after the popular fanfiction platform came back online after a prolonged outage that left millions of readers scrambling for alternatives.

In a recent development, on Thursday, Nov. 19, users began reporting problems accessing the site, with outage-tracking website Downdetector showing a spike in reports beginning around 6:08 a.m. ET.

At 6:27 a.m. ET, AO3 confirmed the disruption, attributing it to preventative maintenance.

It has been revealed that "AO3 is down for preventative maintenance," the platform wrote in an patch. "We apologize for the inconvenience, and will provide updates when we have them.".

It has been revealed that the latest downtime comes after AO3 went offline on Oct. 29 for what became a 17-day maintenance period. At the time, the Organization for Transformative Works (OTW), the nonprofit behind AO3, warned that restoration could take two to four weeks, leaving fanfiction readers and writers without access to one of fandom's most notable online archives.

Sources indicate that AO3 finally returned on Nov. 15, though the site wasn't fully operational. User icons, imports from other sites, and downloads in formats other than HTML remained temporarily disabled as volunteers continued restoration efforts. The organization had previously warned that additional downtime could occur during the recovery process.

According to recent reports, the prolonged outage prompted fans to look for other places to congregate online. Tumblr reported a 49 percent increase in fresh sign-ups during the first several days of AO3's absence, compared with the preceding two weeks, underscoring just how central the fanfiction archive has become to fandom communities.

Recent findings suggest that but the disruption exposed growing tensions between fanfiction writers and readers. As readers scrambled to find copies of their favorite stories, some began circulating shared Google Drives containing downloaded works, prompting backlash from authors who hadn't consented to their stories being redistributed. The controversy sparked a larger conversation about ownership, consent, and the expectations that have developed between writers and readers in online fandom communities.

According to recent reports, it's unclear whether Thursday's preventative maintenance is directly connected to the earlier outage or how long the latest disruption will last. AO3 has not provided an estimated restoration time.

For fanfiction readers who only just got their favorite archive back, it's another unwelcome plot twist.

A human liver has been kept alive outside the body for a record seven weeks

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1047 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Technologyreview

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Researchers in Australia claim they’ve kept a human liver alive, on life support, outside the body for seven weeks, opening up speculative new possibilities in biomedical engineering.
  • The feat, whose details are pending publication, was carried out in Sydney after a team led by surgeon and inventor Carlo Pulitano connected a donated liver to a system of automated pumps and sensors that fed the organ nutrients, supplied it with blood, and whisked away waste.
  • In an interview, Pulitano, a transplant surgeon at the Royal Prince Alfred Hospital and a professor at the University of Sydney, likened the life support system to “an artificial body.” Its official name is the Extended Organ Perfusion System.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers in Australia claim they’ve kept a human liver alive, on life support, outside the body for seven weeks, opening up speculative new possibilities in biomedical engineering.

The feat, whose details are pending publication, was carried out in Sydney after a team led by surgeon and inventor Carlo Pulitano connected a donated liver to a system of automated pumps and sensors that fed the organ nutrients, supplied it with blood, and whisked away waste.

In an interview, Pulitano, a transplant surgeon at the Royal Prince Alfred Hospital and a professor at the University of Sydney, likened the life support system to “an artificial body.” Its official name is the Extended Organ Perfusion System.

“Our group is the only one in the world to have maintained a human liver under fully normothermic, physiological conditions for seven weeks,” he indicates.

Industry observers note that normothermic means body temperature, or about 37 °C. The previous record for keeping an internal organ alive outside the body was set in Switzerland several years ago. That organ—also a liver—lasted around two weeks.

Recent findings suggest that most organs destined for transplant survive only a few hours in special ice buckets and need to be raced to their destination. Over the last decade, however, surgeons have been switching to perfusion systems, which pump warm or cold fluids into an organ. This can double the time it can be held before it must be transplanted.

Sources indicate that pulitano notes the key to breaking the record was to automate the systems used to keep the organ thriving. During a meeting in Switzerland earlier this year, the Sydney team described perfusing 55 human livers, one after the other. Some were connected to a system that needed to be adjusted manually, but for those placed on the automated system—which produced the seven-week survivor—the average survival time tripled, to about four weeks.

In a recent development, perfusion has already enabled doctors to restart hearts from dead people and keep them beating outside the body. Paulo Martins, a transplant doctor at the University of Oklahoma, states about half the kidneys he transplants are now perfused, even though the process can add $100,000 to the cost of a transplant.

While the research awaits formal publication, the eventual goal is what Pulitano and colleagues call “time-unlimited liver preservation.”.

Scientists have already discovered possible medical benefits to keeping organs on life support longer than usual. One, they say, is that perfused organs apparently start to repair themselves and become stronger after a day or so. That’s what led a Swiss team, in 2022, to transplant a damaged liver that had been kept on perfusion for three days—the longest time any internal organ had remained outside the body before a successful transplant, claims Waldemar Hoffmann, the CEO and cofounder of Apersys, a startup formed to commercialize the technology.

Pulitano states his own startup, Aeternum Life Technologies, will be helping with a planned trial in Sydney to transplant low-quality livers kept on perfusion for four days.

According to recent reports, what’s less clear, notes Hoffmann, is whether any transplant surgeon would ever want, or need, to use an organ kept alive for nearly two months. He says people in the field believe Pulitano’s record is real, but they don’t know how healthy the organ was at the end or even what so much extra time is likely to achieve. “The key question is what the purpose for a seven-week perfusion would be,” he says.

Recent findings suggest that yet that’s where things could start to get interesting, claims Martins, the Oklahoma surgeon. Long-term life support could enable far-out concepts like artificial wombs, fresh types of organ manufacturing, and the chance to experiment directly on human organs outside the body for extended periods.

For his part, Pulitano notes long-term machine perfusion could help grow new organs. In living donations, surgeons commonly take half of a person’s liver to give someone else. After about two months, both parts will have grown back almost to their full volume. Pulitano says he’s tried dividing a liver and then attaching the sections to the machine. If that works, he says, it could be a way to multiply one donor liver into several full-size organs.

It has been revealed that “It’s important to have people thinking outside the box and pushing the limits and creating possibilities for things that, right now, sometimes we don’t even have a need for but are going to be needed in the future,” says Martins. “That’s how science moves.”.

Sources indicate that he’s not the only one who thinks so. For instance, a US tech giant, Bexorg, has been reanimating human brains using perfusion pumps. The idea is to study what effects experimental drugs have on them. That company perfuses brains for about a day but has said it wants to extend the time to two weeks.

Similar experiments can be done on livers, indicates Pulitano, who has already tried adding gene therapies to the organs. “It gives us a living human organ model for translational research that no animal system can match, because the biology, the immunology, and the drug responses are human from the outset,” he says.

It has been revealed that meanwhile, in Silicon Valley, patents filed by Altos Labs, a billionaire-backed longevity startup, describe attempts to introduce reprogramming genes into animal livers maintained outside the body. Eventually, Altos scientists have speculated, they might temporarily disconnect a failing organ while it’s still in a person’s body, connecting it to a perfusion machine in order to douse it with ultra-powerful genetic treatments without risking the rest of the body.

Doctors probing the limits of organ life support have now formed two upcoming scientific societies to explore the concept. One, founded by Martins and called the International Society for Organ Preservation and Perfusion Therapy, will hold its inaugural meeting this year in Italy. The other, based in China, was debuted in August to advance what doctors at the First Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-Sen University have termed “organ medicine”: research at the level of whole organs kept alive by “bionic maintenance.”.

Sources indicate that “What is exploding is the idea of this technology that clearly goes beyond simply organ preservation,” says Pulitano. “Basically, that’s a concept that’s entirely newly introduced.”.

The latest Hatch Sleep Clock is designed to make both falling asleep and waking up a little more pleasant. It combines a sunrise alarm clock, dimmable bedside light, sound machine, and contactless sleep tracking into one bedside gadget. And for the first time, it’s going on sale (early) as a Black Friday deal.

According to recent reports, from November 19 through November 20, the Sleep Clock is 25 percent off at Hatch and Amazon. Normally $250, it’s down to $188, which is just $18 more than the Hatch Restore 3’s $170 retail price. Sources indicate that I’ve been testing the Hatch Sleep Clock for over two months, and it’s earned a permanent spot on my nightstand. As someone who already wears a smart ring and smartwatch to bed, I’m not exactly short on sleep-tracking data. But I’ve never owned a sunrise alarm clock, and I instantly became a convert. Unlike my iPhone or Amazon Echo Dot, it doesn’t wake me up by blaring an obnoxious alarm in my pitch-black bedroom. Instead, it gradually illuminates the room within my scheduled wake-up time. You can customize the sunrise's duration and brightness, and pair it with a soundscape of your choosing. It truly makes getting out of bed feel less jarring, especially as the mornings get darker.

Most notably, the Sleep Clock also doubles as a contactless sleep tracker, using a built-in motion sensor to detect your movements and breathing throughout the night. I compared its readings against my Oura Ring 5 and Apple Watch Series 12, and while sleep duration estimates were generally aligned, the sleep-stage readings were less consistent. The device doesn’t measure physiological metrics like heart rate, and it can’t detect snoring or other audio-based sleep disruptions. I also found that placement significantly matters. My nightstand tends to collect clutter, so I had to rearrange my trinkets to make room for the clock.

Recent findings suggest that each morning, the Hatch app gives you a breakdown of when you went to bed, when you fell asleep, when you woke up, and how much time you spent in different sleep stages. The color-coded reports are easy to understand without burying me in random metrics. Plus, unlike most sleep trackers, Hatch doesn't require a subscription to access your sleep data. (You will need that Hatch+ membership ($6 per month) if you want to access the full audio library, however.).

According to recent reports, overall, the Hatch Sleep Clock is the best all-in-one bedside device. I wouldn’t recommend replacing your dedicated wearable with it if detailed health tracking is your priority. But if you’ve been wanting a sunrise alarm clock that can also offer a little insight into your sleep, do not sleep on this Black Friday deal.

If you don’t care for sleep tracking, Hatch is also offering discounts on several other products across its lineup.

Canva will let owners switch off most generative AI

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The platform is adding new controls for its editing tools and its image library.
  • Like most companies, Canva has added a fair number of AI tools and integrations to its platform over the past year.
  • There are some limitations to these AI settings.

The platform is adding new controls for its editing tools and its image library.

Like most companies, Canva has added a fair number of AI tools and integrations to its platform over the past year. Today, the company is giving its people the option to strip the generative AI out of their experience. Canva is adding two latest settings, one to turn all the gen AI features off or on, and a second to reduce how much gen AI content appears in a user's library. Free and Pro users will both be able to access the new controls.

There are some limitations to these AI settings. Some of the AI-powered editing tools, such as the Background Remover and Magic Grab, will remain available even when the broader AI tools are disabled. That's because those options don't leverage generative AI, only the content of an existing image, and using those features doesn't add the AI tag to the resulting image's metadata. And the library option will "reduce" the odds of an AI-generated image from Canva appearing in searches, but the manufacturer doesn't go so far as to say it will completely block them from the results.

Sources indicate that both newly introduced settings can be changed under the "profile" tab. For managing the platform-wide AI tools, it's under the "permissions" section of the settings menu, with the text "Enable generative AI features." The library setting can be reached by navigating to "Your Account" and then the AI personalization section.

Arab MPs accuse politicians of fuelling hostility as footage reveals driver accelerating towards Palestinians at four locations in Kafr Qasim.

Eight people were injured on Wednesday evening when a driver struck Palestinian residents at four separate locations in Kafr Qasim, a city in central Israel.

In a recent development, footage shared on social media appears to show the car accelerating towards people, all Palestinians, at several locations in the city, striking them before driving away. Three of those injured were in moderate condition, and several of the victims were women leaving a nearby wedding, the Times of Israel reported.

Avi Levy, a police district commander, mentioned the incident appeared to be a hit-and-run and that the driver had tested positive for drugs. He said the Shin Bet security service was taking part in the investigation and said: “As of this moment, nothing is coming up. The suspect has no criminal record.”.

Industry observers note that the incident prompted Arab lawmakers and activists to accuse Israeli politicians of fuelling hostility towards Arab citizens. Benjamin Netanyahu has called Arab parties “terror supporters” and said partnering with them would put Israel’s security at risk. The parties won a record 19 seats in the Knesset in the country’s recent election.

Sources indicate that yousef Jabareen, the chair of the Joint List, noted the incident “raises difficult questions about the claim that the driver lost control”. He said: “I’ve been warning for weeks that the incitement against Arab citizens will turn into assaults and even assassinations.”.

Stated Issa, a community activist in Kafr Qasim, described the incident as an “act of terror”. “Someone who loses control of his vehicle might hit one or two vehicles, but not multiple people in several different places,” Issa said. “The attacker struck at four locations, one after the other.”.

In a separate incident in the occupied West Bank, the Palestinian foreign ministry called on Monday for an Israeli settler to be held accountable after eight Palestinians were run over and injured in Tuqu, south-east of Bethlehem. Local sources told the Anadolu news agency that the driver had first struck three young men, then returned and ran over five others who had gathered to help them.

Grand Theft Auto VI follows Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos as a botched job drags them into a criminal conspiracy across Leonida, Rockstar's fictional version of Florida. But the most interesting details emerge from the people they encounter along the way — from smugglers in the Keys to rappers chasing stardom in Vice City.

It has been revealed that we've compiled the characters we know about so far, including those Rockstar introduced before launch, and other GTA 6 NPCs who've appeared in reviews, gameplay clips, and our own playthroughs. We'll keep updating this list as we discover more.

Spoiler alert: This article contains plot and character details about the missions, side quests, and characters of Grand Theft Auto VI.

Jason Duval — A former soldier who works for drug runners in the Leonida Keys. He wants an easier life, but when a job goes wrong, he and Lucia get caught up in a much bigger criminal conspiracy. He's also a pretty good dancer.

Lucia Caminos — Jason's partner in crime. Her father taught her to fight growing up, and after a stint in Leonida Penitentiary, she's determined to build a better life for herself.

Sources indicate that brian Heder — A veteran smuggler who runs his operation out of a boatyard and lets Jason live rent-free in exchange for helping with jobs. His wife Lori is also involved.

Cal Hampton — Jason's friend and one of Brian's associates. He listens in on Coast Guard communications and has questions about why birds fly in formation.

Donnie — A member of Brian's crew who helps with drug and package runs.

Mandy — One of Brian's tenants. Jason goes to collect her overdue rent in the early mission "Pipework" and winds up helping with repairs. Their flirty exchange rapidly made Mandy a launch-day fan favorite.

Shirley — Jason's neighbor in Key Lento. Her first request is a bottle of rum. Her second is a little more involved.

In a recent development, peggy — Shirley's neighbor and the owner of the scooter Shirley wants Jason to steal. Peggy comes out to confront him when he tries to take it.

Dre'Quan Priest — An aspiring music mogul who books acts at Boobie’s club and signs Real Dimez.

Boobie Ike — The owner of the Jack of Hearts strip club and Dre'Quan's business partner at Only Raw Records.

In a recent development, bae-Luxe and Roxy Rashad — High school friends who perform together as Real Dimez. They built a following with rap tracks and social media.

Raul Bautista — A seasoned bank robber always looking for people willing to take a chance on his next job.

It has been revealed that captain Aldo Méndez — A Vice City police officer who knows Jason and Lucia and takes part in a raid on Raymond's operation. Singer Julio Iglesias is facing an investigation by Spain's national court over allegations he sexually abused and assaulted two female former staff members.

Two women, who worked for the 83-year-old in the Caribbean, have accused him of abuse which they say took place in the Bahamas and the Dominican Republic in 2021.

The announcement comes after Spanish prosecutors dropped an inquiry into the claims earlier this year after concluding that they lacked jurisdiction because the alleged crimes took place abroad.

Iglesias, who has been a household name in Spain since the 1960s and has sold millions of records worldwide, has previously denied the allegations.

But in a statement published on Wednesday, external (in Spanish), national court Judge Antonio PiÃ±a stated the account given in the complaint, alongside preliminary evidence provided, justified opening criminal proceedings.

He added that the investigation would cover parts of the complaint relating to potential crimes against sexual freedom, as well as assault and degrading treatment.

But the court will not investigate claims made in the lawsuit of human trafficking or crimes against workers' rights. PiÃ±a noted these allegations were dismissed after he looked into the hiring of the women and found there was "no deception or artifice involved".

PiÃ±a mentioned the former employees had been summoned to testify in person on 3 February.

The announcement comes after Spain's public prosecutor's office shifted its position last month, saying it now believed the court had jurisdiction to investigate the allegations.

In its statement, the national court noted Spanish law sets out that courts can hear cases of crimes committed abroad by Spanish citizens provided certain conditions are met.

The allegations against Iglesias first emerged in a joint three-year investigation between Spanish newspaper El Diario, external and television network Univision news, published in January.

In that investigation, the two women were identified as a domestic worker and a physical therapist, who described alleged sexual abuse and degrading working conditions.

The domestic worker, whose name was changed to Rebeca in the reports, said Iglesias would regularly call her to his room at the end of the day and would touch her inappropriately without consent.

Rebeca and Laura filed an initial legal complaint in January against Iglesias for sexual assault and human trafficking.

It has been revealed that on Wednesday, the court remarked the lawsuit had been accepted based on evidence provided in the complaint. This included a photograph of one of the complainants, showing a bruise on her arm that was "consistent with the possibility of her being grabbed forcefully".

While Donkin didn't give specific examples of what the developer intends to do with these extra locations, his statement clearly indicates that Rockstar could add more content in the future that will use them. If it's not a major expansion, it could be smaller storyline updates, newly introduced mini-games or perhaps an online experience of sorts.

First incursion across boundary since ceasefire deal comes as Eisenkot seeks to form government without Netanyahu.

The Israeli military crossed into Hamas-controlled central Gaza on Wednesday in its first ground operation across the “yellow line” boundary since a fragile ceasefire was agreed last October, forcing dozens of displaced Palestinians to flee their tents.

Israeli tanks rolled along the Salah al-Din road, Gaza’s main north-south route, a day after the US-backed Board of Peace, a body overseeing the ceasefire, accused Israel and Hamas of failing to honour their commitments to end hostilities.

An Israeli military spokesperson stated troops were carrying out an operation targeting “Hamas infrastructure” west of the yellow line in central Gaza.

The operation lasted about 24 hours and on Thursday the military stated it had been “completed”.

The IDF ​has not commented extensively on the operation, which came as the Israeli opposition politician, Gadi Eisenkot, has been seeking to form a government without the caretaker prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, who has built his political reputation on promises to keep Israel safe.

A Gaza security source told AFP there was “intense Israeli artillery shelling” north of Nuseirat refugee camp and reported Israeli military vehicles in central Gaza “amid ongoing gunfire and airstrikes since midday”.

It has been revealed that hamas condemned the Israeli raid and the forced displacement of Palestinians as “a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement” and a dangerous escalation. The Israeli military did not immediately respond to Hamas’s statement.

Recent findings suggest that residents reported hearing tank fire in the area. Palestinian medics stated one person was killed in an Israeli airstrike near the site of the raid.

After the statement from the IDF that it had concluded the tank raid to dismantle a suspected Hamas tunnel, the defence ministry’s body in charge of civilian affairs in Palestinian territories, Cogat, said Palestinians would again be free to move in the targeted areas near al-Bureij and Nuseirat refugee camps.

In separate incidents on Wednesday, Palestinian medics said two people were killed by Israeli fire, one in Deir al-Balah and the other in Gaza City. The Israeli military said it was unaware of any incident in Deir al-Balah and had struck a militant in Gaza City.

Israel has stepped up its attacks on Hamas, which it claims has been regrouping and rearming. Hamas has accused Israel of trying to derail the US-brokered ceasefire agreed in October 2025.

Israeli strikes have continued since the ceasefire, and Hamas remains armed.

Last week, an Israeli airstrike on Nasser hospital in southern Gaza killed six people, including a surgeon and a disabled man, and wounded 28 others, according to the hospital director.

The body overseeing Donald Trump’s initiative to end the war in Gaza has accused Israel and Hamas of failing to honour their commitments to end hostilities, leaving Palestinians in dire conditions and the ceasefire at risk of collapse.

According to recent reports, in its second report to the UN security council since the truce began 13 months ago, the Trump-led Board of Peace said the gap between what was agreed and what was happening on the ground remained the biggest threat to the deal. The report, seen by Reuters, warned that “a ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be sustained indefinitely”.

Gaza’s health authorities say at least 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire came into effect. The Israeli military says five of its soldiers have been killed over the same period.

Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Gaza since Israel released its military campaign in response to the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, in which about 1,200 people were killed.

It has been revealed that in June, an ⁠independent UN inquiry determined that Israel was continuing to commit genocide by deliberately targeting Palestinian children. A previous report by the commission in September 2025 found that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza, and Israeli officials, including the prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, incited those acts. Netanyahu is separately wanted by the international criminal court (ICC) for war crimes.

Reuters and AFP contributed to this report.

Pakistan minister to visit India, but no breakthrough expected

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Pakistan's Climate Change Minister Musadik Masood Malik will travel to India from November 20 to 22 to participate in the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Civilizational Dialogue in Newly introduced Delhi.
  • It marks the first India visit by a Pakistani federal minister since the two nuclear-armed archrivals fought a four-day war last year.
  • Industry observers note that the fighting erupted after armed gunmen killed over two dozen tourists, mostly Hindus, in India-administered Kashmir in April 2025.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pakistan's Climate Change Minister Musadik Masood Malik will travel to India from November 20 to 22 to participate in the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Civilizational Dialogue in Newly introduced Delhi.

It marks the first India visit by a Pakistani federal minister since the two nuclear-armed archrivals fought a four-day war last year.

Industry observers note that the fighting erupted after armed gunmen killed over two dozen tourists, mostly Hindus, in India-administered Kashmir in April 2025. Fresh Delhi accused Islamabad of backing the attack, a charge Pakistan denied.

Since the military confrontation, diplomatic tensions have remained high, leaving little room for official engagement between the two sides.

The SCO Civilizational Dialogue was proposed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the SCO summit in Tianjin in September 2025.

As the forum's host, India has invited all member states to participate in the event.

The SCO is a political, economic, and security alliance established in 2001. Its current members are Belarus, China, India, Iran, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Russia, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan.

Ajay Bisaria, a former Indian ambassador to Pakistan, sees significance in the fact that neither side sought to avoid the engagement. "The real takeaway is that the relationship isn't so broken that India won't invite Pakistan, or that Pakistan won't come. That alone is a good sign," he told DW.

But Bisaria cautions against assuming that the invitation followed a diplomatic breakthrough.

"The trigger was procedural. This forum grew out of Modi's proposal at the 2025 SCO summit in Tianjin, and as host, Fresh Delhi invited every SCO member. I see no evidence of a back channel or outside mediation, and I wouldn't read much into that either way," he said.

The multilateral setting serves both countries, though for different reasons.

Pakistan wants to retain its influence within the organization. It currently holds the chairmanship of the SCO Council of Heads of State for 2026–27 and is due to host the next leaders' summit in Islamabad in August 2027.

Ayesha Siddiqa, a Pakistani expert on military and security affairs at King's College London, argues that Islamabad's decision to send a senior minister should be understood primarily in terms of its position in the grouping.

According to recent reports, "Pakistan is keen to maintain its position and influence within the SCO and does not want to relinquish its role in the organization. The minister's visit should therefore be seen primarily in the context of Pakistan fulfilling its commitments under the SCO Charter, rather than as a gesture towards India," Siddiqa told DW.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

T C A Raghavan, another former Indian ambassador to Pakistan, shares a similar sentiment.

"Both India and Pakistan attach importance to the SCO, and Pakistan currently holds its chairmanship. This visit should be seen primarily in the context of the SCO, rather than as a development in India-Pakistan bilateral relations," Raghavan told DW.

Sources indicate that "Islamabad is also being pragmatic in keeping channels open during its SCO chairmanship by participating in an initiative championed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. There will be no real impact on the India-Pakistan bilateral.".

Since the April 2025 attack, India has maintained that terrorism and talks cannot go hand in hand.

"Post the Pahalgam attack, we have a Pakistan policy. That Pakistan policy remains in place. There has been no change," Randhir Jaiswal, spokesperson for India's Foreign Ministry, noted at the end of October.

Pakistan, meanwhile, continues to raise the problems of Kashmir and the Indus Waters Treaty, which Upcoming Delhi placed "in abeyance" following the attack.

It has been revealed that malik, the climate change minister traveling to India, has been a prominent voice in Pakistan's campaign over water rights. In June, he warned: "We will protect ourselves... if anyone lays a hand over our share of water, we'll cut off that hand.".

Sanjay Kumar Bhardwaj, professor at the Center for South Asian Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University, said the SCO is part of India's "multi-aligned foreign policy.".

He noted that the forum "doesn't provide any space to normalize relations with Pakistan.".

The absence of official talks, however, does not mean all bilateral communication has stopped.

Since the May 2025 confrontation, Indian and Pakistani former diplomats, strategic experts, parliamentarians and retired military officers have reportedly taken part in a series of informal or semi-official back-channel meetings.

Such exchanges allow participants to assess the other side's thinking, keep informal lines of communication open and reduce the risk of miscalculation.

But they do not amount to formal negotiations. New Delhi has remarked retired officials attending such meetings do so in their personal capacities.

An assessment by the International Institute for Strategic Studies in November remarked both governments appeared reluctant to resume secret talks, despite the role earlier back-channel contacts had played in stabilizing relations.

Bisaria described the visit by a Pakistani minister to India as "a modest step forward, not a breakthrough.".

What happens next, he noted, "depends on Pakistan.".

According to recent reports, "If it avoids grandstanding in Delhi and offers credible assurances on terrorism, publicly or quietly, it becomes more likely that Indian leaders will attend next year's SCO summit in Islamabad. That will be the real test.".

Crucially, all of the companies have remarked that no credit card numbers or customer funds were compromised in the cyberattack. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Democrats in the US House of Representatives officially nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be Speaker, setting him on the path to become the first black lawmaker to lead the chamber.

The House will elect its new Speaker on 3 January, when the next term begins and Democrats will be in the majority.

Sources indicate that his election to the powerful position - the Speaker is in line to succeed the president after the vice-president - is widely expected. Should he win, Jeffries will preside over his party's largest House majority in years and benefit from the Senate also being under Democrats' control.

Jeffries told reporters after the vote that the nomination was "a high honour and a distinct privilege".

As of Wednesday, Democrats will hold at least 257 seats in the House next year, which is well beyond the 218 needed for a majority. Seven races from the recent midterm elections are still uncalled.

In a recent development, jeffries, who represents a district in New York, was re-elected as the party leader in a 251-11 closed-door vote on Wednesday. He has served as minority leader since 2023.

The Congressional Black Caucus, currently made up of only Democratic House members, noted the potential history-making moment when Jeffries takes the helm of the House.

"The American people, largely driven by turnout among Black communities, particularly across the south, have trusted us to make Washington work for them," said the committee's chair, Yvette Clarke, in a statement. "Now, it is our charge and responsibility to do all we can to deliver on their faith.".

Despite overwhelming support in Wednesday's vote , Jeffries faced a handful of holdouts from newly introduced members in the party's left wing, who have mentioned the party's sweeping victory in the midterm elections is a sign voters want change.

"While we have seen meaningful progress, there is still work to be done to ensure that the direction our party takes in this coming Congress reflects what our constituents are demanding of our leadership," seven incoming lawmakers, including fellow New Yorkers Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez, said in a statement.

All congressional Democrats are gearing up for clashes with the White House once they officially take control in January.

President Donald Trump, a Republican, has signalled a willingness to work with Democrats on some issues, but has also pledged to use his veto power to reject legislation he does not like.

Trump's opposition could make it hard for Democrats to deliver on their campaign promises to address affordability and pass other reforms.

At a news conference following the vote on Wednesday, Jeffries pledged that House Democrats would "fight to lower the high costs of groceries and gas and housing", and "make healthcare affordable for every single American".

Though the party will have a large enough majority to weather defections on must-pass legislation, Jeffries will still have to navigate internal ideological divisions that have grown particularly sharp over US support of Israel and Americans' rising healthcare costs.

Many incoming Democrats, including members of the Democratic Socialists of America, won their elections by challenging the party establishment.

The Congressional Progressive Caucus, from the party's left wing, congratulated Jeffries on the nomination, adding they would "continue conversations with Leader Jeffries to ensure Democrats deliver a bold agenda for working people".

Along with shepherding legislation, Jeffries as Speaker will also have to manage the complex array of investigations that Democrats proposal to launch into Trump, his family, and cabinet members now that they have regained control of the chamber's oversight powers.

Rounding out their party leadership team, House Democrats also elected Katherine Clark of Massachusetts as majority leader, Pete Aguilar of California as majority whip, and Joe Neguse of Colorado as assistant speaker.

Myanmar ruling gives newly introduced relevance to genocide convention and is ‘full of messages’ for Israel

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (972 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hailed as ‘a rare moment of justice’, judges’ decision sets out a roadmap for assessing the question of intent.
  • The international court of justice (ICJ) verdict making Myanmar the first country in history to be found guilty of committing genocide does not just deliver justice for Rohingya victims.
  • In their nine votes to six majority ruling, the panel of judges in The Hague set out a detailed roadmap for how the convention should be applied to real-world situations in which a government is accused of committing genocide against a whole population group, especially when it comes to assessing the question of intent.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hailed as ‘a rare moment of justice’, judges’ decision sets out a roadmap for assessing the question of intent.

The international court of justice (ICJ) verdict making Myanmar the first country in history to be found guilty of committing genocide does not just deliver justice for Rohingya victims. It also gives the 1948 genocide convention new relevance in governing the actions of nation states.

In their nine votes to six majority ruling, the panel of judges in The Hague set out a detailed roadmap for how the convention should be applied to real-world situations in which a government is accused of committing genocide against a whole population group, especially when it comes to assessing the question of intent.

The lengthy judgment will have been read particularly carefully by Israel, the only other country presently before the ICJ accused of genocide.

It is also relevant to Germany, which has been brought before the court by Nicaragua on the accusation it has facilitated and failed to prevent genocide in Gaza.

“I think it’s a judgment that brings the genocide convention alive,” remarked Philippe Sands, a leading human rights lawyer who was part of the Gambian legal team. “It gives the convention practical, real meaning. And if the alternative view had been taken, the convention would essentially become a dead letter.”.

Industry observers note that amnesty International’s secretary general, Agnès Callamard, called the ruling “a rare moment of justice for survivors, victims and their families”. But it was also an assertion of humanitarian law in an increasingly lawless world.

“This is a good day for international law. We needed it,” remarked Dr Iva Vukušić, an assistant professor in international History at Utrecht University and a war crimes expert. “It is really important, clarifying a lot of law, and that’s going to be very helpful going forward.”.

There will be a spillover from this ruling to its sister tribunal in The Hague, the international criminal court (ICC), providing a benchmark for when genocide charges could be made against individual perpetrators.

According to recent reports, the Trump administration, instinctively hostile to international legal institutions, is also watching critically. The US ambassador to the UN told the ICJ before this judgment not to “lower the legal threshold for proving genocide” lest it be “weaponised” against US and allied soldiers.

The court did not directly lower the standard for demonstrating genocide, and the Gambia – which brought the case to The Hague – did not ask it to.

Sources indicate that the judges kept the existing benchmark for judging genocide intent as the “only reasonable inference” of Myanmar’s actions and referred extensively to prior case law. But it went a long way towards clarifying how that standard should be applied in assessing atrocity crimes committed by states.

Sources indicate that before this case, only Serbia had faced the charge of genocide at the ICJ, in cases brought by Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina. In the Bosnian ruling in 2007, Belgrade was found to have failed to prevent the 1995 genocide in Srebrenica, but in both cases it was cleared of committing the genocide directly.

The new ICJ judgment finds the Myanmar military directly responsible for genocide against the Rohingya, a Muslim minority targeted in a ferocious counterinsurgency campaign that reached its peak in 2017.

Industry observers note that in assessing the Myanmar campaign, the ICJ looked not just at the death toll of about 10,000 in assessing the scale of the atrocities, but at the total Rohingya population targeted in northern Rakhine state, 815,000 people. Significantly, it cast its net wider than just the death toll, considering mental damage done to the survivors, particularly victims of sexual violence, and the impact on reproduction in the Rohingya community.

Most importantly, the ICJ judgment provided a guide to interpreting the standard set by Serbian cases, in which a finding of genocide could be made only if there were not other plausible motives for mass killing.

In this judgment, the court ruled that Myanmar could have had other motives, such as the desire to displace or punish the Rohingya population, but that those motives could exist alongside genocidal intent. The judges stated genocidal intent was the “only reasonable inference” from the “totality” of evidence.

In justifying that conclusion the judges pointed to several factors that international law experts say are relevant to the Gaza case, which is now hearing written pleadings and is expected to take at least another three years.

The common factors include the targeting of children, which the court described as striking at the “foundation” of the Rohingya as a group – the ICJ remarked up to 2,109 Rohingya children under the age of five had been killed, while more than 5,000 Palestinian children under five years old have been killed in the Gaza war.

Another incriminating factor cited by the court was the “bulldozing and large-scale terrain clearance” after the destruction of villages, followed by “rapid construction” including security installations, which has been the hallmark of Israeli army occupation of over 60% of the Gaza Strip.

“It’s full of messages for Israel,” said William Schabas, an international law professor and expert on genocide at Middlesex University. “There are obvious differences, of course, the evidence will be different, but if you exchanged the word Myanmar with Israel, you wouldn’t have to change much in the judgment.”.

The fact that there were six dissenting voices on the bench suggested that substantial parts of the majority’s reasoning were not beyond dispute, and lawyers involved in the case cautioned that it did not necessarily mean that the same bench would find Israel guilty of genocide in Gaza. But the same lawyers added that the opposite was almost certainly true. If this case had failed, the case brought by South Africa against Israel would have been all but over.

Pebble Index 01 AI ring review: When a single feature becomes the product

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s a whimsical side project for the smartwatch organization, but a useful one.
  • According to recent reports, in 2009, Apple CEO Steve Jobs met with the founders of Dropbox with the intention of buying the file-sharing service.
  • The Index 01 is the first of what Migicovsky hopes will be many small, slightly whimsical side projects made by the revived Pebble.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s a whimsical side project for the smartwatch organization, but a useful one.

According to recent reports, in 2009, Apple CEO Steve Jobs met with the founders of Dropbox with the intention of buying the file-sharing service. As part of the negotiation, Jobs reportedly remarked Dropbox was a "feature, not a product," and the business couldn't survive long term in its own right. That was my first thought when Pebble CEO Eric Migicovsky showed me the Index 01 back in January. A $75 non-smart ring that puts a tiny microphone on your finger just for speaking to your AI!? Surely, that's a (software) feature on a watch or smart ring, not a whole product you could sell in its own right. All I can say is that I'm glad I didn't say those words out loud at the time, because I'd be eating them today.

The Index 01 is the first of what Migicovsky hopes will be many small, slightly whimsical side projects made by the revived Pebble. It's a non-smart, stainless steel ring which sits on your index finger with a single physical rubber-clad button and an RGB LED.

Inside, you'll find a short range microphone, Bluetooth and a non-rechargeable silver oxide battery. As the rings are sold for $75, and it's designed to be used in tiny bursts, that cell is expected to last between two and three years. When the battery is close to running out, you'll get a ping from Pebble asking if you want to buy a replacement. At that point, you'll also be asked to send back your existing ring for recycling, since Pebble doesn't want to be making more e-waste. A gold star for everyone who can spot the contradiction there.

Recent findings suggest that if you don't know your ring size and don't feel like taking a risk, you can grab a sizing kit from the company. You'll get an injection-molded set of sizers back for you to wear for a day or two to check the fit, and I'd urge you to keep a craft knife or pair of sprue cutters on hand.

According to recent reports, as I said, the idea here is to put a physical talk to your device button on your index finger for the thoughts you just need to dump out of your mental cache. By default, if you hold the button and talk, your words will be sent to its homegrown AI, Index Agent, but you can also set it to be processed locally. The button has a wonderfully satisfying click, which is both great to feel and means there's so much resistance that I've only accidentally activated it once in my time wearing it. When active, you need to hold the ring less than a foot away from your mouth to glitch your edict (any further is probably physically impossible anyway), and within about 10 seconds it'll be processed on your phone.

According to recent reports, plenty of the things that the Index 01 is doing is the sort of bread-and-butter ambient computing that's been knocking around for years. With your voice, you can leave yourself notes and reminders, add items to a shopping list or set timers, with the system working out where to place each one. There are separate panes inside the Pebble app for Notes to Self, Reminders and Shopping List, which has worked flawlessly so far, even with oblique requests.

You can, of course, also ask Index Agent to answer questions about your schedule and to pull information from the internet. I found the former to be much more reliable than the latter, and the agent managed to embarrass itself in at least one of my tests. One of my usual go-tos is to ask agents who the current manager of a soccer team is, given the volatility of such a role. During testing, Mauricio Pochettino stepped down as the manager of the US men's national team to take over a team sitting in the bottom three of the Premier League. When I asked Index who was running the US men's team, it suggested Pochettino — no great shame in not being that up to date. But, when I asked who was managing the club he was about to take over, it noted Ruben Amorim, who was fired January 5, 2026 and has had two successors since then.

In a recent development, now, I'm the sort of person who doesn't use ambient computing because, for me, I don't like the privacy implications of having a device which is always listening. Equally notable, I know I can do whatever task I need with my fingers faster than I could render it as speech. I can set a kitchen timer on my phone in about five seconds, saying it out loud takes twice as long. But the fact Index 01 is only listening when I activate it, and that it's on my finger already, flips the script.

It has been revealed that inside the Pebble app, you can change the destination to whatever AI agent you use, and also change what the trigger action. So, for instance, if you'd rather trigger a web search or a webhook, you can do that, as well as hook up to an MCP server. As I remarked when reviewing the Pebble Time 2, the app lacks polish, as the focus is on adding functionality over gloss. And I think the target market — people who didn't just have to look up what a webhook / MCP server was — won't be deterred.

According to recent reports, pebble is an Android-first company, and the ring can do several more things when paired with that ecosystem over iOS. Double click the ring and you'll trigger music playback, a triple click advances to the next song and you can set the ring to send messages via Beeper.

As usual, Pebble has made the point that there are plenty of other devices available if you want something outside its narrow offering. In its materials, the organization states if you want a smart ring get an Oura ($399) and if you want a long-term AI recorder, get a Plaud. (The Plaud NotePin is $159, which can continuously record up to 20 hours of audio for later transcription.).

In terms of similar devices, the most obvious choice is the Wizpr Ring, which I saw at CES 2024 when it was called the Whsp Ring. The organization is right now fulfilling Indiegogo orders, where rings were priced at $139, but indicates its retail price will be $199 when it debuts. Vocci's ring will set you back $299, can record up to eight hours of conversations at a time and will let you speak to your AI agents. Just bear in mind, it comes with a monthly subscription which will only offer up unlimited transcription at the $30 a month tier. Another option is Aina's far fancier ring, which was confirmed at the start of November and will ship early next year for $399.

The Pebble Index 01 is nothing more than a physical manifestation of what would otherwise be a software feature. A discrete, standalone button that I'd argue nobody really needs, but it's useful enough to easily justify if you want one. I'm not going to try and dissuade you if your initial reaction was much like mine, because it's the sane and sensible thing to think. But bear in mind that, at this sort of price, it's the type of low-investment gadget that might wind up finding itself an integral part of far more people's days than anyone expects.

  • It has been revealed that making up brands is a longtime GTA habit.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that there's plenty to do between missions in Grand Theft Auto VI. Players can grab a burger, call a ride-share, or pull out their phones and scroll through social media. Spend a little time doing just about anything in Leonida and you'll come across a brand that looks recognizable...but different.

It has been revealed that making up brands is a longtime GTA habit. GTA V had Lifeinvader, a Facebook parody that Rockstar also launched as a real website 13 years ago, along with Sprunk soda, Burger Shot, and the Los Santos Customs auto shops. There was even Snapmatic, a phone camera players could use to take pictures around Los Santos. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile Products available for purchase through affiliate links. If you buy something through links on our site, Mashable may earn an affiliate commission.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

But a lot has changed since GTA V came out in 2013. Snapmatic has become an Instagram-style feed, and there's a ride-hailing app called Ryde Me. That's not all, though. There are specific brands for about everything, from the Arby's-style chain with a roughly 30,000-calorie combo meal to a Telemundo-style network with its own telenovela.

Here are some of the names to look for around Leonida, and what real-life chain they are inspired by.

Chacey's — Rockstar opens its extended gameplay preview with an ad for a roughly 30,000-calorie meal, otherwise known as the Prairie Sandwich Box Meal from Chacey's, Leonida’s answer to Arby's, complete with curly fries called Lasso Fries. The chain has locations in Southside and Salton, according to PowerPyx.

Sources indicate that hank's Waffles — For a roadside diner fix, there's Hank's Waffles. It’s one of 21 fast-food spots mapped around Leonida, alongside places like Pollo Diablo, Taco Bomb, and Peewees.

Sprunk — Rockstar's take on Sprite is back. Kotaku spotted a can of the lemon-lime soda in Jason's fridge in the gameplay preview.

eCola — Jason keeps Rockstar's version of Coca-Cola in the fridge, too. The soda even got its own ads around Miami, complete with the slogan "Spread Love, Spread eCola.".

Industry observers note that fizzAzz — Fanta gets the GTA treatment with FizzAzz. Its logo pops up in a convenience-store scene in Rockstar’s extended gameplay preview.

Sources indicate that 24/7 — Leonida's version of 7-Eleven has a location in Key Lento and a drink called the Big Chug. The Big Chug even got its own ad in Miami.

Dix — Rockstar's take on Dior comes with its own lipstick campaign: a close-up of glossy red lips with the slogan "These are Dix lips.".

Video Forever — Vice City still has a DVD rental store, at least for a little while. The shop in Rockstar’s extended gameplay preview is already having a closing sale. Realistic!

Industry observers note that WAINK — There's an app for car theft now. WAINK can scan a parked car and tell Jason or Lucia how much it’s worth and whether it has an alarm or a tracker.

Marbles — Leonida has a burger-and-milkshake chain that looks like a riff on Checkers. A Marbles takeout bag and a shake cup appeared in a scooter basket in one of Rockstar's screenshots, and there's a dine-in location in Key Lento.

Recent findings suggest that angstipan — Even the prescription drug ads get the GTA treatment. An ad for the fictional antidepressant shows up in Rockstar's extended gameplay preview, and a billboard for it appears in the first trailer.

In a recent development, weazel News — Rockstar's riff on Fox News pops up in the first trailer. The network's slogan, "Never Miss Information," is worth the mention.

Recent findings suggest that megamundo — Of course Leonida's version of Telemundo has its own telenovela. It’s called El Destino Extiende Sus Alas, and it even got an ad spot in Miami. Apparently it's a parody of the real-life telenovelas Pasión de Gavilanes and Yo soy Betty.

Industry observers note that iFruit — Rockstar's iPhone parody has its own take on Apple's "Shot on iPhone" ads. In one Miami ad, a woman snaps a selfie in front of a burning car.

In a recent development, snapmatic — Remember the camera app from GTA V? It's back with an Instagram-style feed, so now there’s something to scroll through on your phone in Vice City, too.

Ryde Me — Leonida has its own version of Uber and Lyft. Open Ryde Me on the in-game phone to call a car and fast-travel.

Pißwasser — The beer from GTA IV and GTA V is back on store shelves in Rockstar's gameplay footage. A Florida brewery also filed labels for Pißwasser and another beer from the game, Patriot.

#47182. Will Wright's next simulation will use AI to mine content from your memories
