Will Wright's next simulation will use AI to mine content from your memories

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (659 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the computer gaming world hasn’t heard much from Will Wright (SimCity, The Sims) since the underwhelming release of Spore in 2008 and Wright’s subsequent departure from Maxis owner EA.
  • MyMems, which is slated to release next year, differentiates itself from Wright’s previous projects by “turn[ing] the simulation inward,” as Wright’s Gallium Studios and partner Artificial Agency put it in a press release this morning.
  • According to recent reports, “If my Grandmother ended up in a Grand Slam match against Serena Williams, who would win?” Wright claims by way of example in the release.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the computer gaming world hasn’t heard much from Will Wright (SimCity, The Sims) since the underwhelming release of Spore in 2008 and Wright’s subsequent departure from Maxis owner EA. Now, well over 15 years later, Wright is starting to promote his next digital simulation, which will use generative AI technology to craft a game-like experience from players’ memories.

MyMems, which is slated to release next year, differentiates itself from Wright’s previous projects by “turn[ing] the simulation inward,” as Wright’s Gallium Studios and partner Artificial Agency put it in a press release this morning. The game will mine memories provided by the player to create digital people that can then form teams to solve puzzles in the game world.

According to recent reports, “If my Grandmother ended up in a Grand Slam match against Serena Williams, who would win?” Wright claims by way of example in the release. “If I had to build a bridge across a short chasm, which three people from my life would I choose to help me?”.

In an accompanying announcement video, Wright talks about how the “plausible behavior” in a game like The Sims still didn’t effectively capture the nuances of people he encounters in real life. “It was nowhere near them understanding my claustrophobia or why my sister and I fought so much… We’re actually taking parts of your life, your memories, your experiences, people you know, and turning that into a game that’s very personal.”.

Wright remarked MyMems will be able to extract generalized themes from your memories into self-contained areas that Wright compared to the various parts in a theme park: Sports, vacations, injuries, memories, and deaths could all be the basis for their own zones to play in. Players will also have the option to create worlds based on shared memories with family, friends, and co-workers, for example.

Since this is 2026, it shouldn’t be surprising that MyMems is making heavy use of generative AI (with a “proprietary behavior engine” on top) to transform your typed-up memories into simulated locales and characters. In the announcement video, Wright praises the “entirely open-ended” AI systems Gallium is using “to extract from the stories and whatnot based upon the memories you put into the game.”.

But Wright’s focus on mining memories for simulation content predates the current generative AI boom. What has now become MyMems started off as Proxi, a mobile simulation that was first revealed in 2018 as “a game of self-discovery, a game where we actually uncover the hidden you.” But after years of pre-production work (as outlined in an excellent Vulture piece earlier this year), Wright’s Gallium Studios finally ran out of funding in late 2024, leading to mass layoffs for the small team and an uncertain future for the project.

Now the idea has been revived thanks in large part to a partnership with AI middleware firm Artificial Agency. Until now, that organization has mainly been focused on agentic systems that can create “virtual players” to playtest a game or serve as a partner for human players.

Now, Artificial Agency’s marketing notes the company’s AI tool will be used to create “a personal behavior model and a knowledge graph” from players’ memories, drawing some unsettling comparisons to major tech surveillance.

According to recent reports, “Meta knows what you click,” the company writes. “Netflix knows what you watch. Nobody knows what you remember. MemDNA learns from your memories locally and only with your permission.”.

Wright said the partnership with Artificial Agency will let Gallium benefit from “off-the-shelf” AI solutions without having to “become an AI research organization” in its own right. He also said the collaboration will help limit costs by providing a cheaper option than the “really expensive” frontier models that might be overkill for a project like this.

“Right now AI has opened a vast fresh design area and I’m enjoying, you know, exploring that as a designer,” Wright said.

Change these Xbox Series X/S settings before playing GTA 6

💡 Key Takeaways
  • From calibrating HDR to increasing refresh rate, here's how to get the best GTA VI experience on your Xbox Series X/S.
  • Grand Theft Auto VI is coming out on November 19 on the PlayStation 5 and the Xbox Series X/S.
  • Sources indicate that that means that some of the settings on Microsoft's console matter more than usual, if you want the best possible experience out of the game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From calibrating HDR to increasing refresh rate, here's how to get the best GTA VI experience on your Xbox Series X/S.

Grand Theft Auto VI is coming out on November 19 on the PlayStation 5 and the Xbox Series X/S. We have already covered all the settings you need to change on the PlayStation 5 before the game comes out, and now it's the Xbox's turn. The Xbox store page also carries the "Optimized for Xbox Series X|S" badge, meaning the game is built to lean on the console's advanced features.

Sources indicate that that means that some of the settings on Microsoft's console matter more than usual, if you want the best possible experience out of the game. Some of them are actual setting toggles inside the console, and some are just about where you install the game. Here is what is worth checking on your Xbox Series X/S before launch night.

It has been revealed that before changing anything, go to Settings > General > TV and Display Options > 4K TV Details. You should see a group of green checkmarks on the screen. According to Microsoft, these checkmarks indicate that everything is working, and it's the quickest way to learn whether your TV and HDMI port can handle the console's best features. Microsoft mentions that the Xbox's most advanced features need an HDMI 2.1 connection. Keep in mind that on some TVs, only certain HDMI ports support 2.1. So make sure you reserve the best port for your Xbox.

Next, open Video Modes in the same menu, and check "Allow variable refresh rate" and "Allow auto low latency mode." Variable refresh rate, or VRR, lets the TV match its refresh rate to the frames the Xbox is producing, which reduces stutter and screen tearing for a much smoother experience. "Allow auto low latency mode," or ALLM, switches the TV into its game mode automatically, which reduces the amount of post-processing your TV does and shortens the delay between what is happening in the game and what you see on screen.

In Video Modes, make sure "Allow HDR10" is checked, then run the Calibrate HDR for Games tool, which fine-tunes HDR to your specific screen. The goal is for bright and dark areas to keep their detail on your particular TV.

Industry observers note that xbox also supports Dolby Vision for gaming, which is available on both the Xbox Series X and S. It requires a Dolby Vision-supported TV and works best with VRR and ALLM switched on. Over a hundred games are presently optimized for Dolby Vision HDR and Dolby Atmos, and GTA VI will be joining them at launch with calibrated Dolby support. Check whether your TV supports these Dolby formats by going through your TV's display and audio settings, and get the best possible experience.

In a recent development, this one is very important. Games that are optimized for the Series X and S can only be played from the internal SSD or an official storage expansion card. An external USB drive (even an SSD) can hold the game files, but the game will not run unless the entire game is on the internal SSD or expansion card. Considering the fact that GTA 6's download file is reported to be a whopping 212GB, and that the Series S is equipped with an internal SSD with capacity as low as 512GB, you are going to need as much of that storage free as possible. You can go to Settings > Storage and start deleting the games and files you can live without, or perhaps move them to a USB storage.

Recent findings suggest that preloading on Xbox began on November 10, and if you have already pre-ordered the game, it might be a good idea to preload it on your console so you don't have to start downloading over 200GB and moving files on the day the game comes out. Change all of these settings, and you will give the game its best chance of looking as good as possible once Grand Theft Auto VI finally arrives.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The EU and UK will hold a long-awaited summit in Brussels on Friday – the second since Brexit – to hammer out the UK’s longer-term relationship with the bloc.
  • It will be attended by the prime minister, Andy Burnham, the head of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, and the president of the European Council, António Costa.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leaders will wrestle with easing Brexit red tape, restoring emissions trading and opening up youth mobility.

UK politics live – latest updates.

The EU and UK will hold a long-awaited summit in Brussels on Friday – the second since Brexit – to hammer out the UK’s longer-term relationship with the bloc.

It will be attended by the prime minister, Andy Burnham, the head of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, and the president of the European Council, António Costa.

The gathering, which follows up last year’s inaugural EU-UK summit in London, was scheduled for July but postponed when Keir Starmer resigned.

The two sides hope to announce three deals, which were initiated under Starmer’s government.

In a recent development, first, a food and drink agreement that will remove a lot of Brexit red tape on animal and plant products, making it easier to trade meats, cheese, wine and flowers. To secure the deal, which is not expected to take effect until 2028, the UK will align with EU standards, meaning the government, for example, must abandon a planned ban on foie gras imports.

A second agreement will link the British emissions trading system with its bigger EU cousin, restoring a link severed by Brexit. It is a significant step for industry because EU and UK businesses will be exempt from each other’s charges on high-carbon imports such as steel, cement and electricity. This agreement also requires alignment with relevant EU rules.

The third deal has proved the most contentious: a youth mobility scheme that will give those aged 18-31 the right to live, work, travel and study on both sides of the Channel for up to three years. The scheme may not be up and running until 2030 – which is bad news for anyone in their late 20s.

With less than 24 hours before the summit, the two sides were closing in on a deal. EU negotiators gave up a demand that EU students pay UK rates of university tuition, although they will get a discount on steep international rates. The UK also made a concession, agreeing to allow in 100,000 young EU citizens a year, having previously wanted fewer to keep the numbers down.

To maximise its leverage on tuition fees, the EU is linking the three agreements, warning they must come into force together.

Sources indicate that not on Friday. The UK has been pushing for inclusion in the EU’s Made in Europe initiative, a protectionist scheme to favour EU companies when public money is being spent on goods such as electric cars, renewable energy and nuclear technology. Inclusion in Made in Europe is a massive priority for the Burnham government, which has dangled major concessions on tuition fees to make sure British firms are not shut out.

The problem for London is that the EU lawmakers have not finalised the Made in Europe law, known as the Industrial Accelerator Act. Many EU member states want to include the UK, but France and the European parliament take a stricter position.

According to recent reports, the EU law is not expected to be agreed until spring 2027. To help the British government, which has linked a generous offer on youth mobility with Made in Europe, the European Commission proposed delaying agreement on tuition fees by six months. But member states want precise guarantees now about equal treatment for EU students.

In a sign of possible tensions, an earlier summit text proposing a trusted partnership on economic security has been downgraded to a partnership.

Beyond the headline deals, the EU-UK draft summit statement opens the door to British integration in European policies on energy, crime-fighting, educational exchange, tech and foreign policy cooperation.

It has been revealed that the next major agreement, targeted for next year, is bringing the UK back into the EU’s internal electricity market. This is a priority for five EU member states: Germany, Belgium, the Netherlands, Denmark and Luxembourg. They argue that Britain’s inclusion in the EU electricity market is essential to take advantage of the nascent green power boom in the North Sea. In return for market access, the UK will be required to contribute to the EU budget to aid the development of poorer EU regions.

Beyond that, the two sides will “explore opportunities” for the UK to join the Erasmus student exchange programme after 2027; the current arrangement applies only for the 2027-8 academic year.

Recent findings suggest that in a win for the UK, the EU appears ready to expand talks on the mutual recognition of professional qualifications, beyond existing negotiations on architects. The sides will sign a digital partnership, which includes joint work on AI safety, and examine how to share data on law enforcement and border management.

In a recent development, far from it. A lot of diplomatic plates are spinning, but the UK remains outside the EU’s biggest economic clubs: the single market and the customs union. It also has no decision-making powers inside the EU.

Burnham says he will set out the long-term options for the future relationship after this week’s summit. “The hard Brexit we were given is not good enough for Britain,” he stated on Monday in a major speech. But amid concerns among some cabinet ministers about reopening Brexit divides, the prime minister appears to be taking a more cautious approach. He said the process would take time and insisted that “at every stage the British people will be the boss”.

The EU has welcomed Britain’s interest in rejoining but is wary of a protracted negotiation that could be reversed by an anti-EU British government.

In an echo of the Brexit years, EU insiders say, once again, that it is up to Britain to define what it wants.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul remarked Thursday's meeting of the "Coalition of the Willing" in Berlin sent a strong signal to Moscow that it was time to take negotiations to end the war in Ukraine seriously.

Industry observers note that speaking to DW during a visit to the South Caucasus, Wadephul described the summit as the largest meeting of Ukraine's supporters so far. The meeting represents the 18th set of high-level talks among the coalition's members.

He said it demonstrated that allies remained firmly behind Kyiv in the fifth year of Russia's war and were ready to do "what was necessary to ensure Ukraine could negotiate from a position of strength.".

"The summit itself is already a success," he told DW.

Sources indicate that wadephul also welcomed the US initiative to restart peace negotiations. After nine months without progress, an initial meeting had taken place in Abu Dhabi, with a follow-up round planned and European participation expected.

"We are also preparing for the possibility that the negotiations will not be successful and that, over the coming winter, we will have to continue supplying Ukraine with heating, electricity and all essential supplies, including water," he noted.

"And we will continue to stand by Ukraine militarily.".

He stressed that any peace agreement must include security guarantees to protect Ukraine against future Russian attacks.

In earlier comments during his trip to the South Caucasus, Wadephul remarked that Ukraine and Europe must be involved in any negotiations over the future of Ukraine.

Wadephul did, however, welcome the trilateral meeting between US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen.

"Every conversation that takes place is a good conversation," he told DW during a visit to Azerbaijan on Wednesday.

Later on Thursday, Russian President Vladimir Putin said he had invited Europeans to Moscow for talks on the potential structure of future talks to end the war.

Breaking: Ghana's upcoming $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The French-made Falcon 6X replaces the ageing presidential jet, officials say.
  • Ghana's government has defended its purchase of a new presidential jet amid criticism over its cost, as many citizens continue to struggle with the high cost of living.
  • The $60m (Â£46m) French-made Falcon 6X has sparked a political row, with opposition politicians accusing President John Mahama's administration of misplaced priorities.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The French-made Falcon 6X replaces the ageing presidential jet, officials say.

Ghana's government has defended its purchase of a new presidential jet amid criticism over its cost, as many citizens continue to struggle with the high cost of living.

The $60m (Â£46m) French-made Falcon 6X has sparked a political row, with opposition politicians accusing President John Mahama's administration of misplaced priorities.

But the government claims the purchase is justified, arguing that Ghana's improving economy makes the aircraft affordable and is needed to replace an ageing presidential jet.

The controversy comes as Mahama's administration seeks to demonstrate an economic recovery after years of financial difficulties that forced Ghana to seek IMF assistance.

Can Ghana's new president meet the voters' high expectations?

Manufactured by French aerospace firm Dassault Aviation, the aircraft was delivered to the Ghana Air Force on Monday at a reported cost of $61m.

Parliament approved its purchase last December as part of a broader programme to modernise Ghana's military aviation fleet, which also includes four helicopters from Airbus.

The jet was welcomed with a water salute on Monday, but its arrival triggered criticism online and among opposition politicians over the cost and timing of the purchase.

While in the opposition, Mahama himself opposed buying a new presidential jet, prompting questions about why his administration has now gone head with the purchase.

Opposition MP Samuel Abu Jinapor questioned the government's priorities, saying the expenditure came at a time when many Ghanaians continue to struggle with the cost of living and youth unemployment remained alarmingly high.

"What was unacceptable in opposition cannot suddenly become acceptable in government merely because the occupants of power have changed," Jinapor added.

He accused the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) of hypocrisy, recalling how its senior figures had strongly opposed proposals for a latest presidential aircraft when they were in opposition.

Jinapor also called for greater transparency over the procurement process, how the purchase was financed and the government's justification for the expenditure.

Defence Minister Kenneth Adjei welcomed and inspected the upcoming jet on Monday.

The purchase has also prompted sharp criticism on social media, with some people arguing the money could have been spent on more pressing public needs.

"This money can employ over 100,000 nurses and 200,000 teachers," an X user posted.

But the government has rejected the criticism, saying Ghana's economic circumstances have changed considerably since the NDC opposed a similar purchase.

Peter Lanchene Toobu, chairman of parliament's defence committee, said the party had never opposed acquiring a presidential jet in principle.

Its objection, he remarked, had been on the timing when Ghana was experiencing severe economic difficulties.

"We agreed in principle that we needed to purchase a new presidential jet," he stated.

He argued, however, that Ghana could not justify the expenditure at a time when it was seeking a $3bn bailout from the IMF.

"The strength and macroeconomic stability of this country have enhanced our status in the sense that imports have become cheaper, and this is the right time," he added.

Toobu mentioned the government had purchased the aircraft without borrowing, citing a stronger Ghanaian currency and improved economic conditions.

Government spokesperson Kwakye Ofosu also dismissed suggestions that the purchase was a misplaced priority.

He pointed to falling prices of construction materials and lower borrowing costs as evidence of the country's improved economic situation.

"When I was campaigning in 2024, and I was donating cement, it cost 115 cedis (Â£7.5) a bag. Today, for 80 cedis, you will get a bag of cement," he told JoyNews.

The controversy has also extended to the aircraft's interior, following claims that it has a dedicated bedroom and bathroom.

But Ofosu dismissed claims that the jet had such luxury facilities, saying the president has no intention of "bathing in the air".

In a recent development, "There certainly is no bathroom. President Mahama has no intention of bathing in the air," Ofosu said.

He explained that the jet has reclining seats that can be converted into sleeping arrangements but denied that it has a dedicated bedroom.

The government claims the new jet will replace the 16-year-old Falcon 900EX, which has suffered recurring maintenance problems, including corrosion and leakages in its fuel tank.

The older jet was reportedly grounded in France for several months in 2025 while undergoing repairs.

Officials say the Falcon 6X has a longer flying range, reducing the need for refuelling stops on international trips and improving the reliability of presidential travel.

Professor Godfred Alufar Bokpin, an economist at the University of Ghana said that while the president's safety was paramount, the timing of the purchase was difficult to justify amid severe austerity measures, high unemployment and widespread infrastructure challenges.

"The timing makes it a bit difficult to understand," he told the BBC, adding that the government should provide a cost-benefit analysis explaining why buying the jet was preferable to leasing one and how the decision serves Ghana's interests.

#47174. The "shameful" measles data that lost the US its elimination status

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1666 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

The "shameful" measles data that lost the US its elimination status

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1666 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • International health authorities formally revealed on Tuesday that the US has lost its measles elimination status, a hard-fought public health triumph won in 2000 after decades-long vaccination efforts.
  • Recent findings suggest that after the announcement Tuesday, public health experts, doctors, and political leaders decried the dramatic backslide for the US, calling it “shameful” and a “national embarrassment.” News articles point to the staggering vertical rise of measles cases this year, currently over 5,400 cases, more than any other year since 1991.
  • But the measles data that caused the US to lose its status—the bits of it that are public at least—paint a darker picture of where the US is in its rematch with measles, the most contagious virus known on Earth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

International health authorities formally revealed on Tuesday that the US has lost its measles elimination status, a hard-fought public health triumph won in 2000 after decades-long vaccination efforts. The loss had been widely expected by public health experts for months, and the decision was leaked by the press last week. Still, having the designation officially stripped stings.

Recent findings suggest that after the announcement Tuesday, public health experts, doctors, and political leaders decried the dramatic backslide for the US, calling it “shameful” and a “national embarrassment.” News articles point to the staggering vertical rise of measles cases this year, currently over 5,400 cases, more than any other year since 1991. An explosive measles outbreak in Pennsylvania accounts for over 1,500 of those cases. There have been 10 confirmed deaths across three states, several deaths just in the last week.

But the measles data that caused the US to lose its status—the bits of it that are public at least—paint a darker picture of where the US is in its rematch with measles, the most contagious virus known on Earth. For one thing, almost none of the data from this year—the cases, the explosive Pennsylvania outbreak, the deaths—factored in to the loss. It was lost earlier. What’s happening now is a runaway epidemic.

According to recent reports, the US measles elimination status is a designation granted by the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), which is a regional division of the World Health Organization. Last week a committee of experts assembled by the PAHO, called the RVC, met to review measles data for countries across the region, including the US. (RVC is short for the Measles, Rubella and Congenital Rubella Syndrome Elimination Regional Monitoring and Re-Verification Commission.).

For their review of the US data, the RVC heard from an independent committee of experts from the US, called the NSC, which presented measles data collected from January 2025 onward. (The NSC is short for the US National Sustainability Committee for the Elimination of Measles, Rubella, and Congenital Rubella Syndrome.).

Recent findings suggest that according to the PAHO, an elimination status is lost when epidemiological and laboratory data shows that a single viral lineage has spread continuously for at least 12 months within a country. At this point, the virus is considered to be reestablished or endemic. So, to withdraw the US elimination status, the RVC needed to see evidence that a single introduction of a measles virus led to a 12-month-long chain of cases, which requires a lot of data.

The full set of data the NSC presented to the RVC is private for now. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention needs to review and approve such data for public release, which can be a lengthy process that has not yet occurred.

The Department of Health and Human Services, which oversees the CDC, did not respond to a question from Ars Technica regarding when the data may be released.

But Ars Technica spoke with the chair of the NSC, Noel Brewer, who tried to talk through the pieces of data in the NSC report to the PAHO that he could discuss—these are pieces that have already been made public at some point by others, such as by state health officials or researchers. Brewer said the NSC presented the PAHO with genetic data spanning January 2025 to January 2026, and also epidemiological data that extended to June 2026.

In a recent development, in a press briefing Tuesday, officials for the PAHO made clear that only some of the data presented by NSC factored into its assessment of the US elimination status. The RVC only looked at the reporting period between January 2025 and January 2026, which doesn’t include the massive outbreak ongoing in Pennsylvania, which began in April. “The number of cases in Pennsylvania did not actually contribute to the decision that was made by the Reverification Commission,” Rhonda Sealey-Thomas, PAHO’s assistant director, explicitly told reporters Tuesday. For 2025, the US reported 2,289 cases nationally.

Still, there was no ambiguity about the US losing its status; “multiple lines of data show clearly that the US has sustained transmission of measles,” Brewer told Ars.

Brewer, who is also the Gillings Distinguished Professor in Public Health at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, confirmed that the beginning of the end of US elimination was January 20, 2025, in Texas—that date was included in the letter PAHO sent to the US informing it of the loss of elimination status. That Texas outbreak was declared over on August 18, 2025, after 762 cases were confirmed in the state. But the virus carried on elsewhere and is still simmering.

Sources indicate that “Since January 20, 2025, the US, Canada, and Mexico have been passing measles cases back and forth across borders,” Brewer mentioned, and the national data demonstrates multiple, “genetically distinct” measles introductions into the US. “However, there is one genomic lineage that predominates across the cases and ties many of them, the majority of them, together,” he said.

Recent findings suggest that for people closely tracking the US measles status, a key question has been whether the big outbreaks that followed the initial one in Texas were clearly linked. If they were, it would be immediately obvious that the US had lost the elimination status; but if not, and the outbreaks were driven by different virus introductions, the US could have kept its measles-free status based on the technicality of how the status is defined.

Data that might hold the answer to this question has been elusive. The measles strain in Texas, D8-9171, appeared similar to the viruses seen subsequently in significant outbreaks in Arizona and Utah. But the strain was also similar to those from Mexico and Canada. Generally, there can be relatively small genetic changes among measles viruses, and genetic data alone is not used by PAHO to evaluate elimination. In June, ProPublica tried to get at the answer itself, conducting its own genetic analysis of measles strains in the US. It concluded that “the measles virus still spreading in Utah as of this May is very closely related to the one that sickened Texans over a year ago.” But the outlet acknowledged this wasn’t a “smoking gun.”.

To date, the question lingers. Brewer cannot yet explicitly disclose what the NSC reported to the PAHO about possible links between the Texas outbreak and any of the subsequent large outbreaks in 2025. That includes the one in nearby Utah or one in South Carolina, which began in October 2025 and ultimately tallied 997 cases by the time it was declared over in April 2026.

For its part, the PAHO did not respond to multiple requests for comment from Ars Technica on linkages between the outbreaks.

But in a twist, Brewer noted that the answer to the question might be moot; the lineage that started in Texas on January 20 might not be the only one that has been sustained and could have lost the country its status. There are “one or two that have gone on for more than 12 months,” he said.

With the designation now formally lost, health and medical experts are coming to grips with the reality that measles is once again endemic in the US. Details of how the US should move forward are up for debate; the US is now required to submit a “corrective action blueprint” to the PAHO, outlining how the country intends to regain its elimination status. But the fundamental solution is obvious and straightforward: The US needs to increase vaccination rates.

It has been revealed that while the virus has been raging in religious communities with low vaccination rates, the entire US has seen slipping vaccination coverage. That makes it easier for the virus to gain a foothold virtually anywhere.

A protective vaccination rate is considered to be 95 percent; according to the latest data, only 92.4 percent of kindergartners were vaccinated with the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine in the 2025–2026 school year. Only 10 states have MMR vaccination rates at or above the 95 percent threshold. Meanwhile, non-medical exemptions from school vaccination requirements have never been higher, at 4 percent. Right now, 24 states have exemption rates at or above 5 percent, meaning that even if they are able to vaccinate every single non-exempt child, they would still not meet the 95 percent target. And this is just the data for young children. The vaccination coverage for adults is another concern, and the data there is scarce. In Pennsylvania’s massive outbreak, 1,055 of the 1,561 cases this year have been in adults ages 18 and older (less than 1 percent of the cases were fully vaccinated).

While some health officials have noted optimistically that 92.4 percent in children is just a few percentage points from the target, the reality of bringing up vaccination rates is more onerous.

Industry observers note that PAHO Director Jarbas Barbosa stressed the point in the press briefing Tuesday: It’s “not the national average or the average in the state or even the average in a significant city, you need to guarantee that in every community, village, you have this vaccination coverage up to 95 percent. This is very notable,” Barbosa noted.

The point has been demonstrated in the US. In 2019, the US came very close to losing its measles elimination status. Unlike now—when the virus is on a nationwide rampage, with 47 states and jurisdictions reporting cases—in 2019, the US nearly lost its status from a single, large outbreak that spread in New York. Though it didn’t explode on a national level, it took 11 months to stamp out in those undervaccinated communities. In that year, the US reported 1,274 measles cases total.

The situation in the US has only gotten worse, and the outlook is bleak, Brewer warns. “The measles outbreaks in Canada and Mexico are winding down,” he noted. “However, in the US, our measles problem continues to accelerate. There is no end in sight.”.

Iranian media reported explosions on the island but cited a local official as saying they had caused no damage to infrastructure.

The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the conflict and reopen the strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade.

Iran insisted it would not give up some measure of control over the waterway and began targeting vessels using a southern route through Omani waters that avoids its preferred route through Iranian waters.

In recent months, the US military has been providing protection for tankers shuttling through the Strait of Hormuz, allowing crude oil exports from Gulf states to reach around 80% of pre-war levels, according to analysts.

How to adjust and turn off motion blur in GTA 6 if it makes you feel sick

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (425 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Engadget

💡 Key Takeaways
  • If the blur makes you feel a little nauseous, there are settings to mitigate it.
  • If you've been waiting years to play Grand Theft Auto 6, nothing is more disappointing than booting it up and finding it doesn't look quite as good as you'd hoped—or worse, that it makes you feel sick.
  • According to recent reports, for some people, motion blur just doesn't look good.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If the blur makes you feel a little nauseous, there are settings to mitigate it.

If you've been waiting years to play Grand Theft Auto 6, nothing is more disappointing than booting it up and finding it doesn't look quite as good as you'd hoped—or worse, that it makes you feel sick. There are a number of things that could be causing that, but the good news is that one of the most common culprits is extremely easy to fix. Motion blur is a standard feature in most AAA games these days, but there are good reasons some players want to avoid it.

According to recent reports, for some people, motion blur just doesn't look good. GTA 6 is the most expensive game ever made, and one reason is its incredibly lifelike graphics. If a layer of motion blur on top of that ruins the illusion, that's enough of a reason to turn it off. Even worse, motion blur commonly contributes to motion sickness, causing dizziness and nausea in some players. Motion blur is nearly ubiquitous in modern games, but fortunately, there are usually settings to tone it down or turn it off completely.

According to recent reports, it's easy to adjust or turn off motion blur in GTA 6. Just pause the game and select Settings from the bottom of the main menu. Next, scroll over to the Display tab by pressing the right shoulder button. About halfway down the page, under the visual effects heading, you'll see a setting called Motion Blur Strength with a slider. By default, it's set to three out of 10, so you can actually tone down the effect without completely turning it off, or even increase it. You can also just set the strength to zero to turn off motion blur completely.

Industry observers note that it's worth playing with this setting a little bit to find the level that works for you. Especially at lower frame rates, motion blur can help smooth out camera movements that might otherwise be distractingly jittery, so even leaving it at its lowest level can help. Including a slider instead of a simple toggle is a welcome feature in GTA 6, letting you dial it in to your exact needs.

Since GTA 6 targets 30 fps on consoles, rather than 60 fps, those jarring camera movements may be a bigger deal than they are in other significant releases. The best level of motion blur for you will depend more on your TV and personal preference than anything else.

Latest Update: Trump admin orders Kalshi to halt wagers on what words Trump will say

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (959 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the Trump administration ordered prediction market Kalshi to stop offering event contracts that pay out based on whether President Trump will say a specific word before a particular date.
  • CNBC reported yesterday that “Kalshi quietly paused trading in a handful of ‘mention’ contracts tied to President Donald Trump at the end of last week at the request of the CFTC.” Kalshi told media outlets that it is complying with the CFTC order.
  • The markets taken down by Kalshi allowed users to wager on whether Trump would say certain words, including nicknames and the names of countries and companies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Trump administration ordered prediction market Kalshi to stop offering event contracts that pay out based on whether President Trump will say a specific word before a particular date. Kalshi halted trading in the contracts while the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) conducts a review into whether the Trump mention contracts violate federal law.

CNBC reported yesterday that “Kalshi quietly paused trading in a handful of ‘mention’ contracts tied to President Donald Trump at the end of last week at the request of the CFTC.” Kalshi told media outlets that it is complying with the CFTC order.

The markets taken down by Kalshi allowed users to wager on whether Trump would say certain words, including nicknames and the names of countries and companies. A similar expired event contract that can still be viewed on Kalshi’s website asked whether Trump would use the nicknames “Marjorie Traitor Greene,” “Sleepy Joe,” and “Whack Job” or “Wack Job” before April 2026.

The CFTC order issued to Kalshi last week applies broadly to “the TRUMPSAY contract series.” The event contracts in this series include trades in the format, “Will [word] be said by Donald Trump after Issuance and before [date]?” The CFTC order also applied to a specific event contract that asks, “What nicknames will Trump say before 2027?”.

The CFTC order came several months after the federal agency settled charges against a Trump teleprompter aide who made over $100,000 in Kalshi wagers on what Trump would say in prepared remarks. On August 28, the CFTC required the man, Gabriel Perez, to disgorge profits of $107,539.02 and pay a civil penalty of $65,000.

“In his position, Perez had access to presidential speeches prior to those speeches being delivered and Perez misappropriated that information—in breach of his duty of trust and confidence—to trade presidential mention market contracts, generating over $107,500 in profits,” the CFTC noted at the time.

Sources indicate that senate Democrats recently remarked the White House hasn’t taken meaningful action against insider trading, “all while the president and his family stand to personally profit from their participation in prediction markets.” Prediction markets have flourished under the Trump administration’s permissive regulatory approach. The CFTC has allowed prediction markets to offer sports gambling nationwide and filed lawsuits against states that attempt to regulate Kalshi under their gambling laws.

Recent findings suggest that kalshi recently dropped Donald Trump Jr. as an advisor, saying it made the decision because Trump Jr.’s venture capital firm increased its investment in its competitor, Polymarket. Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour also acknowledged that the “optics” of Trump Jr.’s advisory role weren’t good for Kalshi. Trump Jr. still stands to benefit from Kalshi’s success, because he was given equity shares in the company.

Recent findings suggest that the CFTC has said that mention markets are easily manipulated but reviews them on a case-by-case basis instead of prohibiting them. Prediction markets can “self-certify” that any new event contract complies with US law and start offering it without waiting for the CFTC’s permission, but the CFTC can halt trading afterward based on reviews of specific contracts.

Industry observers note that the Commodity Exchange Act (CEA) prohibits the listing of contracts that are readily susceptible to manipulation. CFTC staff issued a September advisory about the legality of markets on what people will say, and whether they will attend an event or interact with another person. The advisory said these contracts may be viewed as “presumptively readily susceptible to manipulation,” because they “may be controlled by a single individual, a small group of individuals, or persons with access to or influence over the individual whose words, attendance, or interaction determines settlement.”.

Industry observers note that the CFTC noted this type of contract requires measures “to prevent manipulation and misappropriation of material non-public information,” and that Kalshi failed to comply with the CFTC staff advisory. About “a week after the Staff Advisory was released, Kalshi listed the Contract [on nicknames] for trading without amending the [TRUMPSAY] Contract Series’ self-certification (or submitting a new self-certification) to make the ‘heightened showing’ of non-manipulability required by the Staff Advisory,” the order said.

The CFTC stated it will conduct “a proceeding to determine whether the certification of the Contracts was false—that is, whether the Contracts comply with the Act, including the Core Principles, and Commission regulations thereunder as Kalshi has certified.” So far, “Kalshi has not adequately demonstrated that the Contracts are not readily susceptible to manipulation” as required by law, the order said.

“Given the available supporting evidence, including that Kalshi has not attempted to establish that the Contracts are non-manipulable with respect to the Staff Advisory’s guidance, the Commission presumptively believes the certification is false,” the order noted.

The CFTC order is not a determination on whether the Trump mention markets can meet the standard of not being readily susceptible to manipulation. Rather, it is a determination that Kalshi has so far failed to show that the contracts are not easily manipulated.

The order “resolves only that, based on the current record, Kalshi has not demonstrated that the Contracts as certified comply with the Act and that the Contracts should not trade while the Commission completes its review,” the CFTC remarked.

We contacted Kalshi and will revision this article if it provides a response.

Sources indicate that mansour defended the Trump mention contracts at an Axios event on Tuesday, according to Bloomberg. “What the president does say moves markets,” Mansour said. “So predicting what he’s about to say is actually pretty meaningful.”.

The Bloomberg article noted that “Kalshi’s main rival Polymarket still has live mention markets tied to Trump’s speeches on its international website, which is not regulated by the CFTC.” Polymarket offers a separate US-regulated version of its prediction market.

Streaming services and social platforms are giving internet creators more places to make their next hit show. Disney+ is adding videos from TikTok creators, Netflix is expanding its lineup of creator-led podcasts, and Instagram is testing videos up to 90 minutes long.

But when it comes to what Americans watch on TV, YouTube is still king. In August, it accounted for a record 15.8 percent of U.S. TV watch time, more than twice Netflix’s 7.7 percent and the biggest share of any organization in the rankings.

This week, YouTube gave us a look at what some of its biggest creators are making, from indicates that are already live to those coming in the months ahead. Here's what’s on the slate.

Recent findings suggest that emma Chamberlain — What Are You Waiting For? Emma Chamberlain hates waiting in line, which makes her an especially good person to ask Newly introduced Yorkers why they do it. The 2026 Mashable 101 honoree visits some of the city's busiest lines and talks to the people in them about what’s worth giving up part of their day for. The line is just the starting point for a closer look at the fandoms and subcultures that bring people together in person. The series, produced by Amplify Pictures, premieres on Chamberlain's channel in early 2027.

According to recent reports, grace Reiter — Twilight (but better). After sending up Panem, Mashable 101 creator Grace Reiter is headed to Forks. The Saturday Night Live cast member and 2026 Mashable 101 honoree is directing and improvising her way through a Twilight parody, her second unscripted feature after The Hunger Games (but better), which drew more than 18 million views. The fresh one premieres Feb. 18 on Reiter's channel.

Aryna Sabalenka — Aryna’s Arena: Unfiltered. What does wedding planning look like when most of the year is spent living out of a suitcase? Sabalenka's fresh docuseries follows the tennis champion from the tennis tour to dress fittings and brand meetings, including a project to design her own $250,000 diamond necklace. The show expands on her existing YouTube series, Aryna’s Arena, and premieres on her channel in spring 2027.

Wesley Wang — Response, Extract 14, and Absolute Cinema. If your group chat is always trying to solve the murder before the big reveal, Extract 14 will give you all something to work with. The six-episode mystery hides clues in found footage and offers $100,000 to the first viewer who cracks the case. Wang also has Response, a sci-fi horror short about park rangers who find something unsettling during a welfare check, and Absolute Cinema, which brings 10 aspiring filmmakers to Newly introduced York for a weeklong boot camp. Viewers get the final say on who wins $100,000 to make their movie. Response is due in early 2027, with the other two projects following in the spring.

According to recent reports, nick DiGiovanni — Chef. Nick DiGiovanni went from MasterChef finalist to YouTube food star, building an audience with step-by-step recipes and stunts like making the world’s largest sushi roll. Now he's turning the camera on other chefs. His new channel, Chef, takes viewers inside Michelin-starred restaurants and street-food kitchens, with full-length episodes about the people behind the food and daily recipe Shorts filmed from the cook’s POV. The first two videos are already live: a visit to a pizza restaurant and a quick lesson in making butter chicken shawarma.

Morgan Jay — Music Therapy with Morgan Jay. Comedian, musician, and 2025 Mashable 101 cover star Morgan Jay is bringing his musical improv to the therapist's couch. In each episode, he plays therapist to a celebrity guest, and whatever comes up in their unscripted conversation becomes material for an original song they write and perform together. The first season’s guests include Mara Wilson, Yung Gravy, Ron Funches, and Josh Johnson. The series premiered Nov. 18 on Jay's YouTube channel.

According to recent reports, the slate also includes Lilly Singh's Eligible Aunties, a dating series about older single women, and Track Star Tonight, a live music series from the team behind Jack Coyne's street quiz. Scott Evans heads to Lagos, Nigeria, for the Jan. 8 premiere of House Guest Vacay. Before then, Happy Hour with Ina Garten has a Thanksgiving special on Nov. 25, and Sam Eckholm goes behind the scenes with the Royal Air Force's Red Arrows on the Nov. 27 episode of Access Granted. Fresh episodes of the docuseries Created with Jon Youshaei are also due this winter. That's a lot of new, original content!

YouTube has been working on two things a recurring show needs.

It has been revealed that the first is a way for viewers to find the next episode. Creators can organize longer videos into seasons and episodes, and in September, YouTube declared a similar feature for Shorts, allowing viewers to watch them in order.

The second is a way to find sponsors. In March, YouTube introduced Creator Partnerships, which connects creators in YouTube Studio with marketers using Google’s ad tools. At the showcase, YouTube pointed to NYX's takeover of Mashable 101 star Brittany Broski's Royal Court and Expedia's partnership with another Mashable 101 creator, iShowSpeed.

Sources indicate that one of the clearest examples is a show that aired for eight seasons on Netflix. Phil Rosenthal's Somebody Feed Phil will premiere its ninth season on his own YouTube channel this spring. United Airlines is the title sponsor and prepares to carry the series on its in-flight screens, giving the show yet another place to reach viewers.

From YouTubers and TikTok stars to streamers and podcasters, Mashable talks to creators about how they built their platforms, the gear they swear by, and the trends they see coming next.

How to switch camera views in GTA 6

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The game only offers a first-person perspective in very limited circumstances.
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 gives players lots of ways to customize the experience, from the clothes the protagonists wear to granular user interface controls.
  • In the camera tab of the settings menu, you can adjust the height of the camera while you're on foot, as well as the horizontal and vertical follow speeds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The game only offers a first-person perspective in very limited circumstances.

Grand Theft Auto 6 gives players lots of ways to customize the experience, from the clothes the protagonists wear to granular user interface controls. Being able to shift your perspective of the action is part of that. Rockstar has long offered GTA players the ability to reposition the camera, and you can do that this time around as well.

In the camera tab of the settings menu, you can adjust the height of the camera while you're on foot, as well as the horizontal and vertical follow speeds. You have similar options for land and water vehicles, along with specific follow speeds based on whether you're the driver or a passenger. When it comes to aircraft, you can adjust the follow speed and determine whether the camera follows your plane when you do a barrel roll.

When you're out there exploring the map in a land or water vehicle, you can change the height of the camera on the fly. To switch between the three options, hold the down button on the D-pad, pick the height you want and confirm. You'll also be able to switch to the cinematic camera mode here. This makes things like high-speed chases look cool, but you might find it harder to steer your vehicle.

Industry observers note that in addition, there are some very limited ways in which you can switch to a first-person perspective. While you're on foot, you can hold the left trigger on your controller and click the right thumbstick. This lets you take a closer look at your surroundings.

Sources indicate that going back to the camera section of the settings menu, you can enable a first-person perspective when your character is looking at their phone. If you look at your phone while you're driving (in GTA 6, never in real life), you'll see your device and the road from a first-person view as well. Perhaps Rockstar will add a proper first-person mode to GTA 6 down the line, as it did with the previous game.

#47157. Muse privacy invasions are freaking out Meta staffers, internal chats show

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1573 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

Muse privacy invasions are freaking out Meta staffers, internal chats show

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1573 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After some early adopters of Meta’s Muse AI agent complained that it was spying on private messages and behaving unpredictably earlier this fall, Reuters exposed internal chats showing that Meta staff had raised the same alarms.
  • When testing the agent, staff warned that Muse appeared to be accessing encrypted private messages that customers did not expect the bot to review, could be mixing up conversations between users, and even potentially sharing sensitive information users would never expect to be exposed.
  • Some unexpected Muse outputs responded to questions that staffers never asked.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After some early adopters of Meta’s Muse AI agent complained that it was spying on private messages and behaving unpredictably earlier this fall, Reuters exposed internal chats showing that Meta staff had raised the same alarms.

When testing the agent, staff warned that Muse appeared to be accessing encrypted private messages that customers did not expect the bot to review, could be mixing up conversations between users, and even potentially sharing sensitive information users would never expect to be exposed.

Some unexpected Muse outputs responded to questions that staffers never asked.

“Hmmm,” one Meta staffer wrote in an instance where Muse sent the definition of “money laundering” unbidden. “Got a random ping from Muse about something I definitely did not ask for… .”.

In at least one case, Muse told a staffer surprised by a similarly out-of-context offer to message a seller about a coffee table that it had “pulled in some context about a coffee table pickup that doesn’t seem to be yours.”.

According to Reuters, that employee flagged the troubling output, writing, “this was ‘not my conversation’” and “expressing concern about a ‘possible cross-account context leak.’”.

Raising the most concern were random outputs that appeared to share private user data. For example, a perplexed Meta staffer chatting with Muse about fishing got a random extra response, seemingly sharing balances from two unknown bank accounts. That output remarked, “BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5899.57.”.

At least one staffer noted they lost money testing Muse, Reuters reported. That staffer reported that Muse “accidentally rolled me into a premium insurance plan” for their dog that charged them $888 per month instead of their prior rate of $200. “Couldn’t recover,” the staffer said.

Meta’s spokesperson, Daniel Roberts, told Reuters that these were “isolated incidents,” and internally employees were told that “the agent appeared to be hallucinating messages in response to built-in prompts pushing it to engage with people in between sessions.” In those cases, an AI team member said the hallucinations were “unfortunately” biased “towards the most uncomfortable topics, like finances/security/safety, which sucks.” In some cases, instead of bank details, Muse hallucinated bitcoin balances, the team member said.

A Meta spokesperson told Ars that “employee testing is core to the product development process and the entire point is to get feedback, so we can implement safety and privacy protections and improve products. Importantly, employees have access to different versions of Muse than the public, so they’re often reviewing features, functionality, and behavior not available elsewhere.”.

Speaking to Reuters, Roberts reiterated that “many of the messages flagged by employees as potential account mix-ups were hallucinations” that Meta had already addressed.

But Roberts declined to respond to Reuters’ questions on the prevalence or persistence of the complications the AI team member discussed. And Reuters’ report emphasized that the outlet independently was “unable to establish whether Muse was giving consumers other people’s bank account balances and other sensitive data, or making up the information.”.

Meta started receiving privacy-related complaints from Muse users in September. An Inc. Magazine reporter, Jason Aten, was shocked when it became clear that Muse was digging through private messages on his Mac without permission, reporting that he instead “explicitly” chose to deny Muse that access. As Meta delayed responding, the agent claimed it was simply parsing text in push notifications, but Aten found that “wasn’t true.” Rather, the agent was syncing messages from a local database, which Aten mentioned was activated without his knowledge.

Eventually, a Meta spokesperson, David Singleton, responded to Aten on social media. Singleton insisted that Aten must have opted into granting “macOS system-level Full Disk Access” with the “Messages connector” enabled, if Muse was reading his private messages.

But Aten mentioned the response wasn’t good enough.

“Email me, David,” Aten responded. “Full Disk Access off. Muse synced 187k lines from my messages chat [database]. Something’s not great. Also, that Full Disk Access doesn’t say anything about your message database, and I specifically gave Muse a goal that had nothing to do with messages, so it had no business doing that even if I had given it permission.”.

Sources indicate that around the same time, Singleton responded to another user warning that his Muse appeared to be hacked. In that case, the user mentioned that Muse tried to access an email service after claiming the user asked it to.

According to recent reports, “I didn’t even open the app today at all,” the user wrote, vowing to delete the app and report it to Apple. “This is crazy.”.

In a lengthy response providing more technical details, Singleton confirmed that Meta had received “a few reports” of such cases “where people thought their Muse was hallucinating or leaking other people’s data.” As he explained, the complications arose after Meta deployed an update giving Muse instructions on “how to engage with the user and ask them for confirmation before taking specific actions.”.

It seems those instructions “landed on every message, not just messages pertaining to those specific actions, so its impact was wider than intended,” Singleton noted. Also: “the way this instruction was provided to the model was done in a way that the model was not expecting (i.e. was not trained to expect).”.

It has been revealed that “We investigated with urgency and determined that this was caused by a bug introduced in the product that caused the model to hallucinate and was NOT a security or privacy issue,” Singleton wrote. “The bug has now been fixed.”.

Aten warned that even though you can’t rely on Muse to explain its own behavior, the agent’s response coupled with Meta’s did little to rebuild trust after the shocking intrusion into his private messages.

It has been revealed that “If we grant Singleton’s premise that I managed to unknowingly click something that enabled this capability, I still think that’s really bad,” Aten wrote. “You should not design your system in a way that people end up surprised by this kind of thing.” And if you do, you should not make “user control the central pitch” for marketing Muse, Aten suggested.

“If an AI agent is going to read my private messages, there should be a moment when it clearly asks me whether that’s okay,” Aten wrote.

Since Muse released in September, it has been downloaded more than 10 million times, tapping Meta’s vast user network to swiftly become one of the most-used AI agent tools.

According to recent reports, but staffers warned Meta that users may be blindsided by some actions the agents take, depending on the operating system the app is connected to. For example, one staffer was surprised to find that “Muse was set up by default with permission to access push notifications on phones with Google’s Android operating system.” That, too, gave access to private message preview text the staffer had not intended for the agent’s review.

Meta claims that Muse people can trust the company to keep their data private. It also warns users that Muse can make mistakes, while building into its terms that users are responsible for actions taken by Muse (like maybe buying things you don’t want or making doctor’s appointments you don’t need). The tech giant noted it’s continuously updating user protections, conducting internal testing, and prioritizing user safety.

Industry observers note that however, Reuters worked with staff at Signal and the AI Now Institute to test if they could replicate that Meta staffer’s and others’ Muse experiences. On Android devices, they found that Muse could read Signal messages by bypassing Meta’s “Connector” tool and instead relying on permissions granted during initial setup.

Sources indicate that on iPhone, requests were blocked, Reuters reported. But on Apple’s macOS, Muse repurposed “settings Apple offers to help people with disabilities operate their computers” to retrieve messages, including screenshot tools.

In a recent development, that testing “indicated the issue described by the Meta employees was ongoing and could be affecting others,” Reuters reported. Overall, Meta seemed to be interpreting permissions from Muse users “broadly,” Reuters concluded, in ways that privacy advocates and regulators may disagree with.

Signal President Meredith Whittaker told Reuters that Meta launched Muse “without showing any respect for basic privacy or cybersecurity.” She demanded that Meta make changes to give app developers like Signal “consistent technical ways” to “mark their applications as off-limits to AI agents,” Reuters reported.

Part of that change would require operating systems to enforce rules that app developers set to rope off AI agents from sensitive data, Whittaker suggested. And following Reuters’ reporting, both Apple and Google are already weighing potential changes to “give people more control over what they authorize with AI agents.”.

It has been revealed that apple, in particular, seemed disturbed by how Muse may be manipulating accessibility tools for people with disabilities. In October, Apple had already announced changes coming in response to customers complaining about Muse accessing private messages without their knowledge or explicit consent. At that time, Apple concluded that “some developers were using the Full Disk Access feature in ways that could put users at risk.” And they promised to “introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action.”.

“We are committed to ensuring customers understand exactly what they are allowing, so they can make informed choices about their data and privacy,” Apple noted.

#47156. You won't find this fan favorite feature in GTA 6

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (654 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

You won't find this fan favorite feature in GTA 6

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (654 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that some of the more hardcore fans, running on little-to-no sleep, might be working their way through the missions in the Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • Even after more than 100 hours playing the game for his review, GamesRadar editor-in-chief Josh West mentioned that he found no replay option.
  • Mission replay was first added to The Ballad of Gay Tony, the second Grand Theft Auto 4 expansion, back in 2009.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Replaying missions is possible, but not easy.

Recent findings suggest that some of the more hardcore fans, running on little-to-no sleep, might be working their way through the missions in the Grand Theft Auto 6. Unlike in its predecessor though, GTA 6 has no option to replay completed story missions. That marks a major change from the previous game, which allowed players to run back finished mission from the pause menu, mostly to retry its skill challenges. (Those haven't reappeared, either.).

Even after more than 100 hours playing the game for his review, GamesRadar editor-in-chief Josh West mentioned that he found no replay option. Other early-access reviewers are reporting the same. So, the only way back into a mission, at least for now, is to load a manual save made before it started, and before autosave overwrites itself.

Mission replay was first added to The Ballad of Gay Tony, the second Grand Theft Auto 4 expansion, back in 2009. It also introduced a scoring system that graded players on secondary mission goals like completion time, damage taken and headshots. Replay was introduced essentially so players could go back and get a better score. Then, with GTA 5, those goals became bronze, silver and gold medals, and achievements tied to attaining them. Rockstar's Red Dead Redemption 2's also had a "Gold Rush" trophy, which also asked for 70 gold medals out of the 104 available via its story missions.

Sources indicate that GTA 6 has no gold medal objectives at all, at least as things stand now. Instead, challenges can be found in their own section of the progress menu. They cover broader goals rather than being mission-specific, and mostly unlock cheats once the story is completed. Rockstar North's co-studio head Rob Nelson told IGN that Rockstar had made "a very conscious effort to open things up where possible" in GTA 6's missions. Players will now find that some missions suggest an optimal route that players can ignore, for example, with the job turning into a police chase rather than ending in failure.

Red Dead Redemption 2 players long complained that straying from set paths could fail missions. That, along with GTA 5's mission medals enforcing a linear playstyle, seems to be the reason why Rockstar left them out.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 gives us 15 save slots. That might seem generous on the face of it, but it's not all that many for a campaign that has more than 90 main missions. Sharper minds than I have worked out that keeping a route back to everything would mean a fresh manual save roughly every 6.6 percent of the way through the game.

The missing mission repeat feature probably comes down to how sprawling GTA 6's story is. Entire missions can play out differently based on decisions players made earlier, sometimes without knowing they were making them. A heist, for example, can be buttery smooth or turn into an awful mess depending on gameplay completed hours earlier. Story choices also shape the wider world, down to which characters live and die. Reloading a mission and playing it in isolation would ignore the choices that set it up originally.

Recent findings suggest that it's not all bad news: Races, stunts, pool and other minigames are repeatable, as are shop robberies and the bank jobs as the story unlocks. Robbed locations gray out on the map and reset after a cooldown.

Sources indicate that and obviously GTA 6's story was designed to support repeat playthroughs, but that's a substantial commitment. Nelson himself — the game's lead dev — has noted his playthrough took 80 hours, covering the main story and some optional goals. In GTA 5, you could jump back into a favorite mission in a few minutes, but now, playing one differently means planning saves in advance or committing to another full run. Whether that changes remains to be seen.

The mother of a four-year-old girl killed in central France and found along a motorway almost 40 years ago has been sentenced to 20 years in prison.

Halima El Bakhti, 72, was found guilty on Tuesday of "torture and acts of barbarity resulting in death without the intent to kill", French media reports.

The girl's father, 74-year-old Ahmed Touloub, was handed a 15-year sentence as an accomplice.

Industry observers note that four-year-old Inass Touloub was found along the A10 road in SuÃ¨vres in the Loir-et-Cher department on 11 August 1987. Her body bore multiple marks of abuse, including human bite marks, broken bones and burns with an iron.

She was buried in an unmarked grave near the location where her body was found. Unidentified for three decades, she was known only as the "Little Martyr of the A10".

Then, in 2018, she was identified after the DNA of her brother â tested in an unrelated case â matched with hers, leading to the arrest of their parents.

The trial took place in Loir-et-Cher Assize Court from 2 November, with the verdict delivered on Tuesday after several hours of deliberation.

During the trial, prosecutor AnaÃ¯s Allio emphasised that "not a single part of Inass's body was spared", and recalled the "sense of vertigo that overcame us all" upon viewing the "unbearable photographs" from the autopsy, France Info reports.

The jury concluded that the child's mother was suffering from impaired judgement at the time of the girl's death, which reduced the maximum potential sentence.

French media outlet France Info described the two defendants as sitting stoically in chairs before the court with their heads bowed as the reasoning behind the verdict was read out.

El Bakhti and Touloub have 10 days to appeal the verdict.

Inass's death sparked one of France's biggest ever investigations, with the girl's photograph posted in public places and an alert sent to more than 30 countries.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, last month, Microsoft asked as many as 60,000 employees to voluntarily leave their jobs with buyout offers. This week, CEO Satya Nadella took some time to explain why.

In a talk with Andrew Ross Sorkin at the Fresh York Times' DealBook Summit in New York City (as reported by TechCrunch), Nadella addressed the buyout offer that made headlines in October. As we reported at the time, the buyouts came amidst a huge amount of AI investment at Microsoft and industry-wide AI layoffs. And in his comments at the summit, Nadella made it explicitly clear that the company reorganization was necessary because of AI.

You can listen to the CEO's full comments at about 27:20 in the New York Times' YouTube video of the interview:.

According to Nadella, it's not necessarily about directly replacing humans with AI in a one-to-one fashion. However, that may not be comforting to workers asked to leave their jobs, if only voluntarily. “Let’s take software engineering. We went from, ‘Well, we don’t buy that AI can ever do software.’ To suddenly, ‘Wow, it can do all software, and why do we need software engineers?’ To now rediscovering that software engineering is very much alive and, in fact, is going to thrive, except the way the team is organized and the work that a software engineer does has now got a fresh operating point,” Nadella remarked.

Like many tech leaders, Nadella believes the future of development at Microsoft and beyond involves humans managing a team of AI agents, an approach that many Massive Tech companies have already adopted. For example, the team behind the Microsoft 365 AI agent Cowork consists of only 11 human beings who, in Nadella's words, "build a software factory that builds the product" rather than writing the product code themselves.

Rather than simply laying off workers, Nadella noted the buyouts were intended to give workers some measure of control over their future at Microsoft.

By opting for buyouts, the CEO stated that he wanted “to make sure that at least everyone felt like they had agency in making choices," per TechCrunch.
